title.zh: 卷二 帝紀第二 世宗景帝 太祖文帝
title.en: Volume 2, Annals 2: Emperor Jing; Emperor Wen
title.raw: 卷二 帝紀第二 世宗景帝 太祖文帝 Volume 2, Annals 2: Emperor Jing; Emperor Wen

sentences.zh: 景皇帝諱師，字子元，宣帝長子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing, taboo name Shi, courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan (Sima Yi).
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, whose personal name was Shi and courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan of Jin.

sentences.zh: 雅有風彩，沈毅多大略。

translations.literal: He had refined bearing and presence, was deep and resolute, and possessed great strategic vision.
translations.idiomatic: He carried himself with quiet distinction—steady, resolute, and possessed of a strategist’s breadth of mind.

sentences.zh: 少流美譽，與夏侯玄、何晏齊名。

translations.literal: In youth he enjoyed a fine reputation, and was ranked with Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he was widely praised, and his name stood alongside those of Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.

sentences.zh: 晏常稱曰：「惟幾也能成天下之務，司馬子元是也。

translations.literal: He Yan often declared, "Only one who apprehends subtle turning points can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; Sima Ziyuan is such a man."
translations.idiomatic: He Yan used to say, "It takes someone who senses the moment before it turns to carry the weight of the realm—and that man is Sima Ziyuan."

sentences.zh: 」魏景初中，拜散騎常侍，累遷中護軍。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu era of Wei, he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and eventually promoted to Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei’s Jingchu years he received appointment as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and rose step by step to Central Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 為選用之法，舉不越功，吏無私焉。

translations.literal: He established methods for selection and appointment; recommendations did not exceed actual merit, and clerks practiced no private favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: He set rules for appointments so that promotions matched real achievement, and his staff could not trade on personal connections.

sentences.zh: 宣穆皇后崩，居喪以至孝聞。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanmu died, he observed mourning for her and was famed for extreme filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Xuanmu’s death, he kept mourning with such scrupulous grief that word of his filial piety spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 宣帝之將誅曹爽，深謀秘策，獨與帝潛畫，文帝弗之知也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was about to execute Cao Shuang, with deep plots and secret stratagems he secretly planned only with the Emperor (Sima Shi); Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao) did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: As Sima Yi readied the strike against Cao Shuang, he laid his plans in the deepest secrecy—working them out alone with Sima Shi—while Sima Zhao was kept entirely in the dark.

sentences.zh: 將發夕乃告之，既而使人覘之，帝寢如常，而文帝不能安席。

translations.literal: On the eve of launching the action he was told; then someone was sent to spy on him—the Emperor slept as usual, but Emperor Wen could not find rest on his mat.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi waited until the night before the coup to inform his son; when he sent men to watch Sima Shi’s quarters, Shi slept soundly as on any other night, while Sima Zhao tossed and could not settle.

sentences.zh: 晨會兵司馬門，鎮靜內外，置陣甚整。

translations.literal: At dawn he assembled troops at the Sima Gate, calming inside and outside, and deployed formations in very good order.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he drew up his forces at the Sima Gate, steadying the palace inside and out and arraying them with flawless discipline.

sentences.zh: 宣帝曰：「此子竟可也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan said, "This son is indeed capable."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi said, "This boy will do after all."

sentences.zh: 」初，帝陰養死士三千，散在人間，至是一朝而集，眾莫知所出也。

translations.literal: " At the outset the Emperor had secretly maintained three thousand bravos, scattered among the people; at this moment they gathered in a single morning, and the multitude did not know whence they had come.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Sima Shi had quietly kept three thousand devoted fighters dispersed through the capital; now they materialized overnight, and no one could guess where they had sprung from.

sentences.zh: 事平，以功封長平鄉侯，食邑千戶，尋加衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, by merit he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Changping with a fief of one thousand households; soon he was additionally appointed General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the coup succeeded he was rewarded with the village marquisate of Changping and a thousand-household fief, and before long was named General of the Guard as well.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝薨，議者咸云「伊尹既卒，伊陟嗣事」，天子命帝以撫軍大將軍輔政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, those who deliberated all said, "After Yi Yin died, Yi Zhi succeeded to his duties," and the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor as General Who Stabilizes the Army and Great General to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: At Sima Yi’s death, court opinion echoed the old line—“When Yi Yin passed away, his son Yi Zhi carried on the task”—and the Wei emperor named Sima Shi General Who Stabilizes the Army and regent in the combined office of Great General.

sentences.zh: 魏嘉平四年春正月，遷大將軍，加侍中，持節、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the fourth year of Jiaping of Wei, he was promoted to Great General, added as Palace Attendant, bearing credentials, supervising all military affairs of the central command and the regions, and recording Director of the Secretariat business.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Wei’s fourth year of Jiaping, he advanced to Great General, was given the concurrent post of Palace Attendant, received the imperial baton, took overall command of central and frontier forces, and assumed control of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 命百官舉賢才，明少長，恤窮獨，理廢滯。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to recommend worthy talent, clarify precedence of young and old, show pity to the destitute and solitary, and straighten out stalled appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed every office to put forward able men, to sort seniority fairly, to relieve the widowed and alone, and to clear the backlog of neglected business.

sentences.zh: 諸葛誕、毌丘儉、王昶、陳泰、胡遵都督四方，王基、州泰、鄧艾、石苞典州郡，盧毓、李豐裳選舉，傅嘏、虞松參計謀，鐘會、夏侯玄、王肅、陳本、孟康、趙酆、張緝預朝議，四海傾注，朝野肅然。

translations.literal: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun supervised the four quarters; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao administered prefectures and commanderies; Lu Yu and Li Feng oversaw selection and appointment; Fu Gu and Yu Song joined in planning stratagems; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji took part in court deliberations; the four seas turned their gaze upon them, and court and countryside stood in solemn awe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun held regional commands; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao ran the provinces; Lu Yu and Li Feng handled personnel; Fu Gu and Yu Song shaped policy; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji sat in on the great councils. The empire’s eyes were fixed on that bench, and a hush fell over both palace and plain.

sentences.zh: 或有請改易制度者，帝曰：「'不識不知，順帝之則'，詩人之美也。

translations.literal: When some requested changes to institutions, the Emperor said: "'Not knowing, not perceiving, following the norms of the Di'—that is what the poets praise."
translations.idiomatic: When voices rose for sweeping institutional change, Sima Shi answered, "The Odes praise the ruler who does not meddle for show but simply follows the pattern Heaven set for the sage-kings."

sentences.zh: 三祖典制，所宜遵奉；

translations.literal: The regulations of the three founding ancestors are what ought to be obeyed and upheld;
translations.idiomatic: The precedents left by the three Wei founders are what we are bound to honor;

sentences.zh: 自非軍事，不得妄有改革。」

translations.literal: unless it be military affairs, one must not recklessly carry out reforms."
translations.idiomatic: and apart from what war demands, nothing should be changed on a whim."

sentences.zh: 五年夏五月，吳太傅諸葛恪圍新城，朝議慮其分兵以寇淮泗，欲戍諸水口。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, summer, fifth month, Wu Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke besieged Xincheng; court deliberation feared he would divide troops to raid Huai and Si and wished to garrison the various river mouths.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, the fifth year, Wu’s Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke laid siege to Xincheng. Ministers worried he would detach columns to strike the Huai–Si line and urged posting guards at every ford.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「諸葛恪新得政于吳，欲徼一時之利，並兵合肥，以冀萬一，不暇復為青徐患也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: Zhuge Ke has newly gained power in Wu; desiring to seize momentary advantage, he masses troops at Hefei, hoping for a one-in-ten-thousand chance; he has no leisure again to become a trouble for Qing and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi replied: Zhuge Ke has just seized the helm in Wu; he wants a quick coup de main, so he is piling everything onto Hefei and gambling on a long shot. That leaves him no bandwidth to threaten Qingzhou or Xuzhou again.

sentences.zh: 且水口非一，多戍則用兵眾，少戍則不足以禦寇。

translations.literal: Moreover the river mouths are not one; if many are garrisoned then troops employed are numerous; if few are garrisoned then it is insufficient to resist bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the crossings are many: garrison them all and you drain the army; garrison too few and you cannot hold the raiders off.

sentences.zh: 」恪果並力合肥，卒如所度。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ke indeed combined strength at Hefei, and in the end it was as he had calculated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke did concentrate on Hefei, exactly as Sima Shi had foretold.

sentences.zh: 帝於是使鎮東將軍毌丘儉、揚州刺史文欽等距之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor sent General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian, Inspector of Yangzhou Wen Qin, and others to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi therefore ordered General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian, Yangzhou Inspector Wen Qin, and others to block him.

sentences.zh: 儉、欽請戰，帝曰：「恪卷甲深入，投兵死地，其鋒未易當。

translations.literal: Jian and Qin requested battle; the Emperor said: "Ke rolls up armor and penetrates deep, casting troops onto deadly ground; his edge is not easy to withstand.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin begged leave to attack, but Sima Shi said, "Ke has marched deep with armor bundled for speed—his men are on ground where retreat is death. You do not blunt that kind of momentum head-on."

sentences.zh: 且新城小而固，攻之未可拔。

translations.literal: Moreover Xincheng is small yet solid; attacking it, it cannot yet be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng is a tight nut: storm it now and you will only bloody your hands.

sentences.zh: 」遂命諸將高壘以弊之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered the various generals to raise high ramparts in order to exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: He told his commanders to entrench on high ground and let time do the work.

sentences.zh: 相持數月，恪攻城力屈，死傷太半。

translations.literal: They faced each other several months; Ke attacked the city and his strength was bent; dead and wounded were more than half.
translations.idiomatic: The standoff lasted months; Ke hammered the walls until his army was spent, with casualties running past the halfway mark.

sentences.zh: 帝乃敕欽督銳卒趨合榆，要其歸路，儉帥諸將以為後繼。

translations.literal: The Emperor then ordered Qin to lead picked troops to hurry to Heyu and intercept his return route; Jian commanded the various generals as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi then instructed Wen Qin to race picked troops to Heyu and cut Ke’s line of retreat, while Guanqiu Jian followed with the main body in support.

sentences.zh: 恪懼而遁，欽逆擊，大破之，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: Ke feared and fled; Qin intercepted and struck, greatly defeating them, beheading more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ke broke and ran; Wen Qin hit him on the withdrawal and shattered his army, taking more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 正元元年春正月，天子與中書令李豐、後父光祿大夫張緝、黃門監蘇鑠、永甯署令樂敦、冗從僕射劉寶賢等謀乙太常夏侯玄代帝輔政。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Zhengyuan, the Son of Heaven with Palace Secretariat Director Li Feng, the empress's father, Grand Master of Splendid Carriage Zhang Ji, Yellow Gate Supervisor Su Shuo, Yongning Office Director Yue Dun, Supernumerary Household Coachman Liu Baoxian, and others plotted to have Minister of Ceremonies Xiahou Xuan replace the Emperor in assisting government.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Zhengyuan year 1, the Wei emperor conspired with Palace Secretariat Director Li Feng, his father-in-law Zhang Ji of the Splendid Carriage rank, the eunuch overseer Su Shuo, Yue Dun of the Yongning office, Liu Baoxian as supernumerary coachman, and others to install Minister of Ceremonies Xiahou Xuan as regent in Sima Shi’s place.

sentences.zh: 帝密知之，使舍人王羨以車迎豐。

translations.literal: The Emperor secretly learned of it and ordered houseman Wang Xian to meet Feng with a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi got wind of the plot and sent his houseman Wang Xian to fetch Li Feng in a carriage.

sentences.zh: 豐見迫，隨羨而至，帝數之。

translations.literal: Feng saw himself pressed and followed Xian and arrived; the Emperor rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Li Feng rode back with Wang Xian, where Sima Shi confronted him with a litany of charges.

sentences.zh: 豐知禍及，因肆惡言。

translations.literal: Feng knew calamity had reached him and therefore let loose evil words.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the noose tighten, Li Feng answered with a torrent of abuse.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，遣勇士以刀鐶築殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and dispatched braves to kill him by striking with the sword ring.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Sima Shi sent brawny guards who beat him to death with the pommels of their swords.

sentences.zh: 逮捕玄、緝等，皆夷三族。

translations.literal: They arrested Xuan, Ji, and others; all were exterminated to the third degree of kin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xuan, Zhang Ji, and the rest were seized and executed along with their entire kin to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 三月，乃諷天子廢皇后張氏，因下詔曰：「奸臣李豐等靖譖庸回，陰構凶慝。

translations.literal: In the third month, then he prompted the Son of Heaven to depose Empress Zhang, and thereupon issued an edict saying: "The traitorous ministers Li Feng and others practiced base slander and secretly formed vicious designs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he induced the emperor to dismiss Empress Zhang and promulgated an edict declaring that Li Feng and his confederates had trafficked in slander and woven a secret web of treason.

sentences.zh: 大將軍糾虔天刑，致之誅辟。

translations.literal: The Great General aligned with Heaven's punishment and brought them to execution.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General, acting as Heaven’s scourge, brought them to the block.

sentences.zh: 周勃之克呂氏，霍光之擒上官，曷以過之。

translations.literal: How does it exceed Zhou Bo's overcoming the Lü clan or Huo Guang's capturing the Shangguan?
translations.idiomatic: What Zhou Bo did to the house of Lü, what Huo Guang did to the Shangguans—this deed matches them and more.

sentences.zh: 其增邑九千戶，並前四萬。

translations.literal: Increase his fief by nine thousand households; together with the previous, forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Let his appanage swell by nine thousand households, for a total of forty thousand with what he already holds.

sentences.zh: 」帝讓不受。

translations.literal: " The Emperor declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi demurred and refused the grant.

sentences.zh: 天子以玄、緝之誅，深不自安。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven because of the execution of Xuan and Ji was deeply not at ease with himself.
translations.idiomatic: The execution of Xiahou Xuan and Zhang Ji left the young emperor inwardly terrified.

sentences.zh: 而帝亦慮難作，潛謀廢立，乃密諷魏永甯太后。

translations.literal: And the Emperor also feared trouble arising and secretly plotted deposition and installation; then he secretly prompted Wei Empress Dowager Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi for his part feared an explosion at court and began laying plans to replace the throne; he quietly sounded out Wei’s Empress Dowager of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 秋九月甲戌，太后下令曰：「皇帝春秋已長，不親萬機，耽淫內寵，沈嫚女德，日近倡優，縱其醜虐，迎六宮家人留止內房，毀人倫之敘，亂男女之節。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month, day jiaxu, the empress dowager issued an order saying: "The emperor's years are already grown; he does not personally attend to the myriad affairs; he indulges in inner favorites, sinks in debasing woman's virtue; day by day he draws near to actors and jesters, letting loose their ugly cruelty; he welcomes six-palace family members to stay in inner chambers, destroying the ordering of human relations, disordering the norms of men and women.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu in the ninth month of autumn the empress dowager proclaimed that the emperor is no longer a child, yet he ignores the business of state, wallows in palace favorites, and tramples womanly virtue; he haunts the company of actors, indulges their outrages, and brings kin from the harem to lodge in the inner apartments—wrecking human decency and turning the sexes upside down.

sentences.zh: 又為群小所迫，將危社稷，不可承奉宗廟。

translations.literal: Moreover he is pressed by a crowd of petty men; he will endanger the altars of soil and grain; he cannot inherit and serve the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Puppeteered by petty flatterers, he is steering the altars toward ruin and is unfit to tend the imperial shrines."

sentences.zh: 」帝召群臣會議，流涕曰：「太后令如是，諸君其如王室何？

translations.literal: " The Emperor summoned the host of ministers to a joint conference and, weeping, said: "The empress dowager's order is thus; what will you gentlemen do for the royal house?
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi then assembled the ministers. In tears he asked, "The Dowager has spoken; what are we to do for the house of Cao?"

sentences.zh: 」咸曰：「伊尹放太甲以甯殷，霍光廢昌邑以安漢，權定社稷，以清四海。

translations.literal: " All said: "Yi Yin banished Taijia in order to bring peace to Yin; Huo Guang deposed Changyi in order to secure Han; they temporarily settled the altars of soil and grain in order to clear the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: They answered in one voice: "Yi Yin banished Taijia to save the Shang altars; Huo Guang cast down the king of Changyi to steady the Han; both took the realm in hand until order returned to the world."

sentences.zh: 二代行之于古，明公當之於今，今日之事，惟命是從。

translations.literal: The two generations enacted it in antiquity; the enlightened lord meets it today; as for today's affair, only your command is followed.
translations.idiomatic: Those two did it in the past; you must do it now. We await your word and will obey.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「諸君見望者重，安敢避之？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: The expectations you gentlemen place on me are heavy; how dare I refuse them?
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi said: You lay a heavy charge on me; how could I shrink from it?

sentences.zh: 」乃與群公卿士共奏太后曰：「臣聞天子者，所以濟育群生，永安萬國。

translations.literal: " Then together with the host of dukes and ministers he memorialized the empress dowager saying: "Your subjects have heard that the Son of Heaven is that by which he succors and nurtures the multitude of lives and eternally pacifies the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he and the high ministers jointly memorialized the Dowager: "We have always been taught that the Son of Heaven exists to nurture the people and give lasting peace to every corner of the realm.

sentences.zh: 皇帝春秋已長，未親萬機，日使小優郭懷、袁信等裸袒淫戲。

translations.literal: The emperor's years are already grown; he has not personally attended to the myriad affairs; day by day he causes petty jesters Guo Huai, Yuan Xin, and others to strip bare and commit lewd play.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is grown, yet he never touches state papers; day after day he sets petty buffoons like Guo Huai and Yuan Xin to strip off and perform obscene farces.

sentences.zh: 又於廣望觀下作遼東妖婦，道路行人莫不掩目。

translations.literal: Moreover below the Guangwang Watchtower he made Liaodong sorceress performances; travelers on the road none did not cover their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the Guangwang Watchtower he staged the lewd "Liaodong hag" skits until wayfarers had to avert their faces.

sentences.zh: 清商令令狐景諫帝，帝燒鐵炙之。

translations.literal: Director of Pure Music Linghu Jing remonstrated with the emperor; the emperor burned iron and roasted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Pure Music director Linghu Jing remonstrated, the emperor had iron heated white-hot and seared him with it.

sentences.zh: 太后遭合陽君喪，帝嬉樂自若。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager suffered the mourning of Lord Heyang, the emperor played and enjoyed himself as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Even while the Dowager mourned the Prince of Heyang, the emperor caroused as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 清商丞龐熙諫帝，帝弗聽。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of Pure Music Pang Xi remonstrated with the emperor; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Pure Music assistant Pang Xi’s pleas went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 太后還北宮，殺張美人，帝甚恚望。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager returned to the North Palace, she killed Lady Zhang; the emperor was greatly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dowager withdrew to the North Palace and executed Lady Zhang, the emperor nursed a bitter grudge.

sentences.zh: 熙諫，帝怒，復以彈彈熙。

translations.literal: Xi remonstrated; the emperor was angry and again used a pellet to shoot Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xi spoke up again, the emperor flew into a rage and pelted him with a slingshot.

sentences.zh: 每文書入，帝不省視。

translations.literal: Whenever documents came in, the emperor did not examine them.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials piled up unread on his desk.

sentences.zh: 太后令帝在式乾殿講學，帝又不從。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered the emperor to lecture on learning in the Shiqian Hall; the emperor again did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The Dowager ordered him to study in the Shiqian Hall; he refused that as well.

sentences.zh: 不可以承天序。

translations.literal: He cannot inherit Heaven's ordering.
translations.idiomatic: He cannot sustain the Mandate’s line of succession.

sentences.zh: 臣請依漢霍光故事，收皇帝璽綬，以齊王歸籓。

translations.literal: Your subjects request, following the precedent of Han's Huo Guang, to seize the emperor's seals and ribbons and return the Prince of Qi to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: We beg leave, on the model of Huo Guang of Han, to take back the imperial seals and send the Prince of Qi home to his fief."

sentences.zh: 」奏可，於是有司乙太牢策告宗廟，王就乘輿副車，群臣從至西掖門。

translations.literal: " The memorial was approved; thereupon the responsible officials with the grand bull sacrifice announced in the ancestral temple; the king took the secondary carriage of the imperial equipage, and the host of ministers followed to the West Ye Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Dowager approved. The proper offices sacrificed the grand ox, read the proclamation at the shrines, and had the king mount the secondary carriage of the imperial train while the ministers escorted him to the West Ye Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝泣曰：「先臣受曆世殊遇，先帝臨崩，托以遣詔。

translations.literal: The Emperor wept and said: "Former ministers received generations of special favor; the former emperor, facing death, entrusted them with the testamentary edict.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi wept and said, "My forebears enjoyed extraordinary favor from the house of Wei; the late emperor, on his deathbed, bound us with his final charge.

sentences.zh: 臣復忝重任，不能獻可替否。

translations.literal: Your subject again shamefully bears heavy responsibility; I was unable to present what is acceptable and replace what is not.
translations.idiomatic: I have disgraced that trust by failing to speak plainly when policy went awry.

sentences.zh: 群公卿士，遠翟舊典，為社稷深計，寧負聖躬，使宗廟血食。

translations.literal: The host of dukes and ministers, citing ancient precedent, for the altars of soil and grain made deep plans, rather burdening the sacred person, so that the ancestral temple might retain its blood sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: You nobles, invoking old precedent and thinking only of the altars’ safety, would rather wrong the person of the emperor than let the ancestral shrines go cold.

sentences.zh: 」於是使使者持節衛送，舍河內之重門，誅郭懷、袁信等。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent envoys bearing credentials to guard and escort, lodged at the heavy gate of Henei, and executed Guo Huai, Yuan Xin, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys with batons escorted the deposed ruler to confinement beyond the inner gates of Henei, while Guo Huai, Yuan Xin, and their ilk were put to death.

sentences.zh: 是日，與群臣議所立。

translations.literal: That day, together with the host of ministers he deliberated whom to establish.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he met his ministers to choose a successor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「方今宇宙未清，二虜爭衡，四海之主，惟在賢哲。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "At present the cosmos within the four seas is not yet clear; the two bandits contend in balance; the lord of the four seas lies only in the worthy and wise.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi declared, "The realm is still unsettled, Wu and Shu strain against us, and whoever sits the throne must be worthy enough to master it.

sentences.zh: 彭城王據，太祖之子，以賢，則仁聖明允；

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Cao Ju, a son of Emperor Taizu—by worth, then benevolent, sage, enlightened, and trustworthy;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pengcheng, Cao Ju, is a son of Cao Cao: in talent he is humane, clear-sighted, and utterly dependable;

sentences.zh: 以年，則皇室之長。

translations.literal: by years, then the eldest of the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: in age he is the senior man of the blood royal.

sentences.zh: 天位至重，不得其才，不足以寧濟六合。

translations.literal: The position of Heaven is extremely heavy; without obtaining his talent, it is insufficient to pacify and succor the six directions.
translations.idiomatic: The throne is too heavy a burden for anyone who lacks his gifts; without him we cannot steady the world."

sentences.zh: 」乃興群公奏太后。

translations.literal: " Then he rose with the host of dukes and memorialized the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: With that he led the senior nobles to the Dowager with a joint memorial.

sentences.zh: 太后以彭城王先帝諸父，于昭穆之序為不次，則烈祖之世永無承嗣。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because the Prince of Pengcheng was the former emperor's various uncles, in the order of zhao-mu was out of sequence, then the generation of Emperor Liezu would forever lack inheriting successors.
translations.idiomatic: She objected that Cao Ju, as an uncle of the reigning line, would break the proper zhao-mu order of the shrines and leave Emperor Ming’s line without heirs.

sentences.zh: 東海定王，明帝之弟，欲立其子高貴鄉公髦。

translations.literal: Prince Ding of the East Sea, Emperor Ming's younger brother—she wished to establish his son, Duke of Gaoguixiang Mao.
translations.idiomatic: She preferred the son of Prince Ding of the East Sea—Emperor Ming’s younger brother—namely Cao Mao, the Duke of Gaoguixiang.

sentences.zh: 帝固爭不獲，乃從太后令，遣使迎高貴鄉公於元城而立之，改元曰正元。

translations.literal: The Emperor firmly disputed but did not obtain; then he followed the empress dowager's order, sent envoys to welcome the Duke of Gaoguixiang at Yuancheng and established him, changing the era name to Zhengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi argued hard but lost the point; bowing to the Dowager, he sent to Yuancheng for Cao Mao, installed him as emperor, and proclaimed the new era name Zhengyuan.

sentences.zh: 天子受璽惰，舉趾高，帝聞而憂之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, receiving the seal, was lazy; lifting his toes high; the Emperor heard and worried about it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cao Mao received the imperial seal he grew careless and walked with a swagger; Sima Shi heard of it and grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 及將大會，帝訓於天了曰：「夫聖王重始，正本敬初，古人所慎也。

translations.literal: When about to hold the great assembly, the Emperor instructed the Son of Heaven saying: "The sage kings value the beginning, correct the root and revere the inception; this is what the ancients were cautious about.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the great court gathering, Sima Shi admonished the emperor: "A true king weighs every beginning, sets the root straight, and treats the first step as sacred—so the classics warn.

sentences.zh: 明當大會，萬眾瞻穆穆之容，公卿聽玉振之音。

translations.literal: Tomorrow there will be the great assembly; the myriad multitude will gaze on august deportment; dukes and ministers will listen to jade-resonant tones.
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow’s levee will put you before every eye—ten thousand pairs of eyes watching your bearing, every minister listening for the ring of true kingship in your voice.

sentences.zh: 詩云：'示人不 佻，是則是效。

translations.literal: The Poetry says: 'Showing others not frivolous—this is the model, this is the pattern to emulate.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Show the people no levity—that is the pattern they will follow."

sentences.zh: '易曰：'出其言善，則千里之外應之'。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'When one's words issue good, then beyond a thousand li they respond.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes adds, "Speak a true word, and the realm answers from a thousand leagues away."

sentences.zh: 雖禮儀周備，猶宜加之以祗恪，以副四海顒顒式仰。

translations.literal: Although ritual and ceremony are complete in every way, still one ought to add reverent scruple, in order to match the four seas' gazing up in hope.
translations.idiomatic: Even with every rite rehearsed, you must layer on humble care, for the whole world is holding its breath toward you.

sentences.zh: 」癸巳，天子詔曰：「朕聞創業之君，必須股肱之臣；

translations.literal: On guisi, the Son of Heaven issued an edict saying: We have heard that a lord who founds an enterprise must have arm-and-thigh ministers;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the emperor issued an edict that they say the founder of a dynasty needs ministers who are his right arm and his thigh.

sentences.zh: 守文之主，亦賴匡佐之輔。

translations.literal: A lord who preserves the written legacy also relies on the assistance of those who set aright and aid.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who only keeps the ledger likewise depends on steady hands beside him.

sentences.zh: 是故文武以呂召彰受命之功，宣王倚山甫享中興之業。

translations.literal: Therefore Wen and Wu by means of Lü and Shao displayed the merit of receiving the mandate; King Xuan leaned on Shanfu and enjoyed the enterprise of the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen and King Wu shone because they had a Lü Wang and a Duke of Shao; King Xuan of Zhou rose from decline because he leaned on Zhong Shanfu.

sentences.zh: 大將軍世載明德，應期作輔。

translations.literal: The Great General for generations bears bright virtue; responding to the period he serves as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General comes from a line steeped in virtue; Heaven’s season set him at my side as helper.

sentences.zh: 遭天降險，帝室多難，齊王蒞政，不迪率典。

translations.literal: Encountering Heaven's sending of peril, the imperial house had many hardships; the Prince of Qi assumed government, not following and leading the canons.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has tried the royal house again and again; the Prince of Qi held power yet would not walk the path the statutes mark out.

sentences.zh: 公履義執忠，以甯區夏，式是百辟，總齊庶事。

translations.literal: The lord treads righteousness and holds fast to loyalty, thereby bringing peace to the region of Xia; he models the hundred lords and aligns the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: You have walked in loyalty and justice, quieted the heartland, shown the hundred officials their pattern, and pulled every thread of government into order.

sentences.zh: 內摧寇虐，外靜奸宄，日昃憂勤，劬勞夙夜。

translations.literal: Within he crushed bandit cruelty; without he stilled treacherous villainy; at sundown anxious and diligent, toiling early and late.
translations.idiomatic: Within the walls you broke the traitors’ grip; on the borders you stilled intrigue; you toiled past sunset and rose before dawn.

sentences.zh: 德聲光於上下，勳烈施于四方。

translations.literal: Virtuous fame shines above and below; meritorious deeds extend to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue lights court and countryside alike; your merit reaches to the four seas.

sentences.zh: 深惟大議，首建明策，權定社稷，援立朕躬，宗廟獲安，億兆慶賴。

translations.literal: Deeply pondering the great deliberation, he first established clear strategy, temporarily settled the altars of soil and grain, raised and established Our person; the ancestral temple obtained peace; the hundred millions rejoice and rely.
translations.idiomatic: You weighed the gravest question, framed the clearest plan, steadied the altars in the crisis, and lifted me to the throne—so the shrines stand unshaken and the people have cause to rejoice.

sentences.zh: 伊摯之保乂殷邦，公旦之綏甯周室，蔑以尚焉。

translations.literal: Yi Zhi's protecting and governing the Yin state, Duke Dan's pacifying and securing the Zhou house—nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: What Yi Yin did for the Shang, what the Duke of Zhou did for the Zhou—your deed stands beside theirs and is not found wanting.

sentences.zh: 朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: We greatly praise this.
translations.idiomatic: I honor you for it with all my heart.

sentences.zh: 夫德茂者位尊，庸大者祿厚，古今之通義也。

translations.literal: Now he whose virtue is luxuriant has exalted position; he whose merit is great has thick emolument—this is the common principle of ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: Great virtue wins high rank; great service wins rich reward—that has been the rule from antiquity to our day.

sentences.zh: 其登位相國，增邑九千，並前四萬戶；

translations.literal: Let him ascend to the position of Chancellor of State, increase fief by nine thousand, together with the previous forty thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Let him be named Chancellor of State, with nine thousand new households added to his fief, for a total of forty thousand including what he already holds;

sentences.zh: 進號大都督、假黃鉞，入朝不趨，奏事不名，劍履上殿；

translations.literal: advance title to Grand Commander, grant the yellow battle-axe, enter court without hurrying, memorialize affairs without naming oneself, sword and shoes on the hall;
translations.idiomatic: advance his style to Grand Commander, lend him the golden yue, let him enter court at an easy pace, memorialize without giving his name, and wear sword and shoes in the throne hall;

sentences.zh: 賜錢五百萬，帛五千匹，以彰元勳。

translations.literal: bestow five million cash and five thousand bolts of silk, in order to display the founding merit.
translations.idiomatic: and grant him five million cash and five thousand bolts of silk, that all may see how the founding merit is crowned."

sentences.zh: 」帝固辭相國。

translations.literal: " The Emperor firmly declined the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi firmly declined the post of Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 又上書訓于天子曰：「荊山之璞雖美，不琢不成其寶；

translations.literal: Again he submitted a letter instructing the Son of Heaven saying: "The uncut jade of Jingshan, though beautiful, if not carved does not become its treasure;
translations.idiomatic: He sent another memorial coaching the throne: "The raw jade of Mount Jing is lovely, yet without the carver’s wheel it never becomes a gem;

sentences.zh: 顏冉之才雖茂，不學不弘其量。

translations.literal: Yan and Ran's talent, though luxuriant, without study does not enlarge their capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Hui and Ran Boniu were gifted men, yet without learning their breadth of mind would never have opened."

sentences.zh: 仲尼有云：'予非生而知之者，好古敏以求之者也。

translations.literal: Zhongni had a saying: I was not born knowing it; I loved the ancients and was keen in seeking it.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said plainly that he was not born wise—that he loved the old lore and pressed himself until understanding came.

sentences.zh: '仰觀黃軒五代之主，莫不有所稟則，顓頊受學於綠圖，高辛問道于柏招。

translations.literal: Looking up at the lords of the five generations from the Yellow Thearch onward, none lacked a model they received; Zhuanxu received instruction from the Green Chart, Gaoxin inquired of the Way from Bai Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Look back to the five sage reigns from the Yellow Emperor: every one of them had teachers—Zhuanxu learned from the Green Chart, Gaoxin took counsel from Bai Zhao.

sentences.zh: 逮至周成，旦望作輔，故能離經辯志，安道樂業。

translations.literal: Down to King Cheng of Zhou, the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao served as assistants; therefore they were able to depart from the classics and distinguish aims, secure the Way and rejoice in their tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Cheng the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao stood at his side, so the heir could move beyond rote text, fix his purpose, find peace in the Way, and take joy in ruling.

sentences.zh: 夫然，故君道明於上，兆庶順於下。

translations.literal: When it is thus, therefore the ruler's Way is clarified above and the myriad common people obey below.
translations.idiomatic: That is how a clear standard shines from the throne and the common folk fall into step below.

sentences.zh: 刑措之隆，實由於此。

translations.literal: The loftiness of punishments set aside truly proceeds from this.
translations.idiomatic: The age when punishments rust unused in the storehouse grows from nothing else.

sentences.zh: 宜遵先王下問之義，使講誦之業屢聞於聽，典謨之言日陳於側也。

translations.literal: One ought to follow the sense in which former kings questioned those below, so that the work of lecturing and recitation is repeatedly heard by the listener, and words of canons and counsels are daily arrayed at one's side.
translations.idiomatic: You should revive the ancient habit of learning from your ministers—let lectures ring often in your ears and let the language of the classics sit daily at your elbow.

sentences.zh: 」時天子頗修華飾，帝又諫曰：「履端初政，宜崇玄樸。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was rather cultivating splendid adornment, and the Emperor again remonstrated saying: At the year's footing and the beginning of government, one ought to esteem plain simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor was already drifting toward display; Sima Shi urged him again: the first months of a reign call for austerity, not glitter.

sentences.zh: 」並敬納焉。

translations.literal: All were respectfully accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne took his advice in good part.

sentences.zh: 十一月，有白氣經天。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month there was white vapor stretching across the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month a pale band of vapor cut the full span of the heavens.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，有彗星見於吳楚之分，西北竟天。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, there was a comet appearing in the Wu-Chu division, in the northwest filling the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, the second year, a comet blazed across the Wu–Chu sector of the sky from the northwest to the horizon.

sentences.zh: 鎮東大將軍毌丘儉、揚州刺史文欽舉兵作亂，矯太后令移檄郡國，為壇盟於西門之外，各遣子四人質于吳以請救。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian and Inspector of Yangzhou Wen Qin raised troops and made rebellion, falsely issuing an empress dowager order and circulating proclamations through commanderies and principalities; they made an altar covenant outside the west gate, each sending four sons as hostages to Wu to request rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian, Grand General Who Guards the East, and Wen Qin, Yangzhou’s inspector, rose in revolt, forged a rescript in the Dowager’s name, sent manifestos across the commanderies, swore a blood oath on a platform west of the walls, and each sent four sons east as hostages to beg Wu for aid.

sentences.zh: 二月，儉、欽帥眾六萬，渡淮而西。

translations.literal: In the second month, Jian and Qin led a host of sixty thousand, crossed the Huai and went west.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month they marched sixty thousand men across the Huai and drove west.

sentences.zh: 帝會公卿謀征討計，朝議多謂可遣諸將擊之，王肅及尚書傅嘏、中書侍郎鐘會勸帝自行。

translations.literal: The Emperor convened dukes and ministers to plan punitive expedition strategy; court deliberation mostly said one could dispatch various generals to strike them, but Wang Su and Director of the Secretariat Fu Gu and Palace Secretariat Gentleman Zhong Hui urged the Emperor to go in person.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi called the high ministers to plan the campaign; most favored sending subordinate generals, but Wang Su, Fu Gu of the Secretariat, and Zhong Hui of the Palace Secretariat pressed him to take the field himself.

sentences.zh: 戊午，帝統中軍步騎十餘萬以征之。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the Emperor commanded the central army infantry and cavalry of more than one hundred thousand to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu he led well over a hundred thousand central-army horse and foot against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 倍道兼行，召三方兵，大會于陳許之郊。

translations.literal: Doubling roads and marching together, he summoned troops from three directions and held a great assembly on the outskirts of Chen and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He forced the march, called in contingents from three directions, and massed them on the Chen–Xu plain.

sentences.zh: 甲申，次於隱橋，儉將史招、李績相次來降。

translations.literal: On jiashen, he halted at Yinqiao; Jian's generals Shi Zhao and Li Ji came to surrender one after another.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen he encamped at Yinqiao, where Jian’s officers Shi Zhao and Li Ji surrendered in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 儉、欽移入項城，帝遣荊州刺史王基進據南頓以逼儉。

translations.literal: Jian and Qin shifted into Xiangcheng; the Emperor sent Inspector of Jingzhou Wang Ji to advance and occupy Nandun in order to press Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels pulled into Xiangcheng, Sima Shi ordered Jingzhou Inspector Wang Ji to seize Nandun and pin Jian in place.

sentences.zh: 帝深壁高壘，以待東軍之集。

translations.literal: The Emperor deepened walls and raised high ramparts, in order to await the gathering of eastern troops.
translations.idiomatic: He dug in behind high walls and waited for the eastern columns to assemble.

sentences.zh: 諸將請進軍攻其城，帝曰：「諸君得其一，未知其二。

translations.literal: The various generals requested to advance the army and attack their city; the Emperor said: You gentlemen have grasped one point but do not know the second.
translations.idiomatic: His generals begged to storm Xiangcheng, but Sima Shi told them they had seen only half the problem.

sentences.zh: 淮南將士本無反志。

translations.literal: The Huainan officers and soldiers fundamentally had no rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan rank and file never wanted this rebellion.

sentences.zh: 且儉、欽欲蹈縱橫之跡，習儀秦之說，謂遠近必應。

translations.literal: Moreover Jian and Qin wish to tread the traces of the vertical-horizontal persuaders, practice the doctrines of Yi and Qin, and think that near and far will surely respond.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Wen Qin fancy themselves wandering strategists in the mold of Su Qin and Zhang Yi; they expect the whole region to rise at their call.

sentences.zh: 而事起之日，淮北不從，史招、李績前後瓦解。

translations.literal: Yet on the day the affair arose, north of the Huai they did not follow; Shi Zhao and Li Ji before and after disintegrated.
translations.idiomatic: When the revolt broke, the north bank of the Huai refused to move, and Shi Zhao and Li Ji melted away in turn.

sentences.zh: 內乖外叛，自知必敗，困獸思鬥，速戰更合其志。

translations.literal: Inner discord and outer rebellion—they know themselves they must be defeated; a cornered beast thinks of fighting; swift battle further fits their intent.
translations.idiomatic: Betrayed within and without, they know they are finished; like beasts at bay they will fight—and a hasty battle is exactly what they want.

sentences.zh: 雖云必克，傷人亦多。

translations.literal: Although it is said one must surely overcome, the wounded will also be many.
translations.idiomatic: We might win a rush attack, but the butcher’s bill would be steep.

sentences.zh: 且儉等欺誑將士，詭變萬端，小與持久，詐情自露，此不戰而克之也。

translations.literal: Moreover Jian and the others deceive and beguile officers and soldiers; their treacherous shifts are myriad; if one slightly persists with them, their deceitful situation will expose itself of itself—this is conquering them without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Jian lies to his own troops and shifts his story by the hour; give him rope and his fraud will show—then we take him without a storm.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣諸葛誕督豫州諸軍自安風向壽春，征東將軍胡遵督青、徐諸軍出譙宋之間，絕其歸路。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Zhuge Dan to supervise Yu Province troops from Anfeng toward Shouchun, and General Who Conquers the East Hu Zun to supervise Qing and Xu troops out between Qiao and Song, cutting off their return route.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhuge Dan with the Yu columns from Anfeng toward Shouchun and Hu Zun with Qing–Xu forces through the Qiao–Song corridor to sever their retreat.

sentences.zh: 帝屯汝陽，遣競州刺史鄧艾督太山諸軍進屯樂嘉，示弱以誘之。

translations.literal: The Emperor encamped at Ruyang and sent Inspector of Yan Province Deng Ai to supervise Taishan troops to advance and encamp at Lejia, showing weakness in order to lure them.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi camped at Ruyang and ordered Yanzhou Inspector Deng Ai to push the Taishan contingents forward to Lejia and feign weakness as bait.

sentences.zh: 欽進軍將攻艾，帝潛軍銜枚，輕造樂嘉，與欽相遇。

translations.literal: Qin advanced the army about to attack Ai; the Emperor secretly moved troops with mouth-gags, lightly went to Lejia, and encountered Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Qin advanced on Deng Ai, Sima Shi slipped an army forward with bits in the horses’ mouths, raced to Lejia, and met Wen Qin head-on.

sentences.zh: 欽子鴦，年十八，勇冠三軍，謂欽曰：「及其未定，請登城鼓噪，擊之可破也。

translations.literal: Qin's son Yang, age eighteen, whose courage crowned the three armies, said to Qin: While they are not yet settled, I request to ascend the wall and beat drums and clamor; striking them, they can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin’s son Yang, eighteen and the fiercest man in the army, urged his father to strike before the enemy settled—mount the wall, beat the drums, raise the battle cry, and they could be broken.

sentences.zh: 」既謀而行，三噪而欽不能應，鴦退，相與引而東。

translations.literal: Having planned then acting, three clamors yet Qin could not respond; Yang withdrew, together they led away eastward.
translations.idiomatic: They put the plan in motion, but after three rounds of shouting Wen Qin never moved; Yang fell back, and father and son drew off toward the east.

sentences.zh: 帝謂諸將曰：「欽走矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the various generals: Qin has fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi told his commanders that Wen Qin was running.

sentences.zh: 」命發銳軍以追之。

translations.literal: He ordered to dispatch picked troops to pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the elite vanguard forward in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「欽舊將，鴦少而銳，引軍內入，未有失利，必不走也。

translations.literal: The various generals all said: Qin is an old commander; Yang is young yet keen; leading the army inward, there has been no loss of advantage; he surely will not flee.
translations.idiomatic: The generals objected that Wen Qin was a veteran, his son young and fierce, and that they had driven deep without a reverse—they would not simply bolt.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「一鼓作氣，再而衰，三而竭。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: The first drum rouses spirit; the second, it wanes; the third, it is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi answered that the first roll of the drum lifts an army’s heart, the second dulls it, and the third empties it.

sentences.zh: 鴦三鼓，欽不應，其勢已屈，不走何待？

translations.literal: Yang thrice drummed; Qin did not respond; their momentum is already bent; if not fleeing, what does one await?
translations.idiomatic: Yang beat the signal three times and his father never moved—their momentum is spent. If that is not flight in the making, what is?

sentences.zh: 」欽將遁，鴦曰：「不先折其勢，不得去也。

translations.literal: Qin was about to flee; Yang said: If we do not first break their momentum, we cannot depart.
translations.idiomatic: As Wen Qin prepared to slip away, Yang warned that unless they blunted the enemy charge they would not break free.

sentences.zh: 」乃與驍騎十餘摧鋒陷陣，所向皆披靡，遂引去。

translations.literal: Then with more than ten swift cavalry he shattered the vanguard and broke formations; wherever he went all were swept aside; then he led away.
translations.idiomatic: He led a dozen picked horsemen in a spearhead charge that scattered every line before him, then broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝遣左長史司馬璉督驍騎八千翼而追之，使將軍樂林等督步兵繼其後。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Left Chief Clerk Sima Lian to supervise eight thousand swift cavalry to flank and pursue them, and ordered generals such as Yue Lin to supervise infantry to follow their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi sent his left chief clerk Sima Lian with eight thousand horse to sweep around Wen Qin’s flank and told generals such as Yue Lin to bring the footsoldiers up behind.

sentences.zh: 比至沙陽，頻陷欽陣，弩矢雨下，欽蒙盾而馳。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Shayang, repeatedly they broke Qin's formations; crossbow bolts rained down; Qin covered himself with a shield and galloped.
translations.idiomatic: By Shayang they had torn through Wen Qin’s lines again and again; bolts fell like rain, and Wen Qin crouched under his shield and spurred on.

sentences.zh: 大破其軍。

translations.literal: Greatly defeated his army.
translations.idiomatic: They shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 眾皆投戈而降，欽父子與麾下走保項。

translations.literal: The host all cast aside halberds and surrendered; Qin father and son with those under their command fled to protect Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The men threw down their weapons and yielded; Wen Qin and his son raced with their remaining followers to the refuge of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 儉聞欽敗，棄眾宵遁淮南。

translations.literal: When Jian heard Qin was defeated, he abandoned the host and fled by night to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian, hearing of Wen Qin’s rout, abandoned his army and fled south into Huainan by night.

sentences.zh: 安風津都尉追儉，斬之，傳首京都。

translations.literal: The Commandant of Anfeng Ford pursued Jian, beheaded him, and sent the head by relay to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant at Anfeng Ford ran him down, struck off his head, and sent it to Luoyang by post-horse.

sentences.zh: 欽遂奔吳，淮南平。

translations.literal: Qin then fled to Wu; Huainan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin escaped into Wu, and the Huainan rebellion was over.

sentences.zh: 初，帝目有瘤疾，使醫割之。

translations.literal: At the beginning, the Emperor's eye had a tumor ailment; he had a physician cut it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Sima Shi had suffered a growth on his eyelid and had had it lanced by a physician.

sentences.zh: 鴦之來攻也，驚而目出。

translations.literal: When Yang came to attack, startled, the eye came out.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Yang’s assault caught him unprepared, the wounded eyeball burst from its socket.

sentences.zh: 懼六軍之恐，蒙之以被，痛甚，齧被敗而左右莫知焉。

translations.literal: Fearing the six armies' terror, he covered it with a quilt; the pain was extreme; he gnawed the quilt until it was ruined, yet those left and right did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid the army would panic, he muffled his face in the bedclothes; the agony was so fierce that he chewed the quilt to rags, and none of his attendants realized what was happening.

sentences.zh: 閏月疾篤，使文帝總統諸軍。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month the illness was severe; he ordered Emperor Wen to overall command the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month his condition turned grave, and he handed overall command of the armies to Sima Zhao.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，崩于許昌，時年四十八。

translations.literal: On xinhai, he died at Xuchang; at the time his years were forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Xuchang on xinhai, aged forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 二月，帝之喪至自許昌，天子素服臨吊，詔曰：「公有濟世甯國之勳，克定禍亂之功，重之以死王事，宜加殊禮。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Emperor's mourning arrived from Xuchang; the Son of Heaven in plain garment attended the condolence; an edict said: The lord had merit of succoring the age and pacifying the state, merit of overcoming and settling disaster and rebellion; doubled by dying in the king's affair; one ought to add extraordinary rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the catafalque reached the capital from Xuchang. The emperor came in mourning white to mourn and issued an edict that he had saved the age and steadied the state, crushed rebellion, and laid down his life in the king’s service—he must be honored beyond the common rule.

sentences.zh: 其令公卿議制。

translations.literal: Let dukes and ministers deliberate the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Let the high ministers frame the rites.

sentences.zh: 」有司議以為忠安社稷，功濟宇內，宜依霍光故事，追加大司馬之號以冠大將軍，增邑五萬戶，諡曰武公。

translations.literal: The responsible officials deliberated that he was loyal and secured the altars of soil and grain, his merit succored within the four seas; it was fitting to follow Huo Guang's precedent, posthumously add the title Grand Marshal to crown Great General, increase fief by fifty thousand households, and posthumous name Duke Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The offices memorialized that his loyalty had steadied the altars and his service had embraced the realm; on Huo Guang’s precedent they asked to stack the posthumous title of Grand Marshal above that of Grand General, add fifty thousand households to his fief, and give the posthumous epithet Wu, meaning Martial.

sentences.zh: 文帝表讓曰：「臣亡父不敢受丞相相國九命之禮，亡兄不敢受相國之位，誠以太祖常所階曆也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen submitted a memorial declining saying: Your subject's deceased father did not dare accept Chancellor of State and the nine bestowals of the minister of state; your subject's deceased elder brother did not dare accept the position of minister of state—truly because Emperor Taizu constantly trod those steps.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao declined in a memorial: his late father had refused the chancellor’s regalia and the nine gifts; his late brother had refused the title of minister of state—because those were the very stairs Cao Cao himself had climbed.

sentences.zh: 今諡與二祖同，必所祗懼。

translations.literal: Now the posthumous name is the same as the two ancestors; this is surely what one reverently fears.
translations.idiomatic: To give him the same posthumous wording as the two Wei founders fills me with dread.

sentences.zh: 昔蕭何、張良、霍光咸有匡佐之功，何諡文終，良諡文成，光諡宣成。。

translations.literal: In the past Xiao He, Zhang Liang, and Huo Guang all had merit of setting aright and assisting; He was posthumously named Wenzhong, Liang Wencheng, Guang Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He, Zhang Liang, and Huo Guang all earned the right to counsel the throne; they were remembered as Wenzhong, Wencheng, and Xuancheng respectively.

sentences.zh: 必以文武為諡，請依何等就加。

translations.literal: If one must use wen and wu as posthumous names, I request to follow He and add accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: If the court insists on pairing wen and wu in the temple name, let it follow Xiao He’s pattern and add only what fits.

sentences.zh: 」詔許之，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it; posthumous name was Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and the dead man was remembered as Zhongwu, Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 晉國既建，追尊曰景王。

translations.literal: When the Jin state was established, he was posthumously honored as Prince Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After the duchy of Jin was founded, he was posthumously raised to Prince Jing.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，上尊號曰景皇帝，陵曰峻平，廟稱世宗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, the elevated honor title was Emperor Jing, the tomb was called Junping, the temple was called Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne, Sima Shi was canonized as Emperor Jing, buried at Junping, and given the temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 文皇帝諱昭，字子上，景帝之母弟也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, taboo name Zhao, courtesy name Zishang, was the uterine younger brother of Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, personal name Zhao and courtesy name Zishang, was Sima Shi’s full younger brother.

sentences.zh: 魏景初二年，封新城鄉侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingchu of Wei, he was enfeoffed village marquis of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei’s second year of Jingchu he received the village marquisate of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 正始初，為洛陽典農中郎將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi, he became Colonel of Agriculture at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengshi era he was named Colonel Director of Agriculture for Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 值魏明奢侈之後，帝蠲除苛碎，不奪農時，百姓大悅。

translations.literal: Encountering after Wei Ming's extravagance, the Emperor remitted harsh minutiae, did not seize agricultural seasons, and the hundred surnames greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: He took office after Emperor Ming’s spendthrift years, scraped away petty exactions, left farmers to their seasons, and the people were delighted.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 大將軍曹爽之伐蜀也，以帝為征蜀將軍，副夏侯玄出駱谷，次於興勢。

translations.literal: When Great General Cao Shuang campaigned against Shu, he appointed the Emperor General Who Conquers Shu, assisting Xiahou Xuan out Luogu Valley, halting at Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang marched against Shu, Sima Zhao was named General Who Conquers Shu and second-in-command to Xiahou Xuan through Luogu, encamping at Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 蜀將王林夜襲帝營，帝堅臥不動。

translations.literal: Shu general Wang Lin night-attacked the Emperor's camp; the Emperor lay firm and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shu officer Wang Lin raided his camp by night, Sima Zhao stayed flat on his couch and never stirred.

sentences.zh: 林退，帝謂玄曰：「費禕以據險距守，進不獲戰，攻之不可，宜亟旋軍，以為後圖。

translations.literal: When Lin withdrew, the Emperor said to Xuan: Fei Yi by occupying peril holds defense; advancing, one does not obtain battle; attacking is not possible; one ought urgently to wheel the army and take it as planning for later.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lin fell back, Sima Zhao told Xiahou Xuan that Fei Yi held the narrows, that they could neither force a battle nor storm him, and that the army should wheel about at once and plan another day.

sentences.zh: 」爽等引旋，禕果馳兵趣三嶺，爭險乃得過。

translations.literal: Shuang and others led the return; Yi indeed galloped troops toward the Three Ridges; contending for peril, then they were able to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang drew off; Fei Yi raced columns to the Three Ridges and only after a sharp fight for the heights did Wei’s army get through.

sentences.zh: 遂還，拜議郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned and was appointed Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was named Gentleman Consultant.

sentences.zh: 及誅曹爽，帥眾衛二宮，以功增邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Cao Shuang was executed, he led a host to guard the two palaces; by merit his fief was increased one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang fell, he commanded the troops that sealed both palaces and earned another thousand households for it.

sentences.zh: 蜀將姜維之寇隴右也，征西將軍郭淮自長安距之。

translations.literal: When Shu general Jiang Wei raided Longyou, General Who Conquers the West Guo Huai from Chang'an opposed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Wei struck Longyou, Guo Huai, the western field commander, marched out from Chang’an to meet him.

sentences.zh: 進帝位安西將軍、持節，屯關中，為諸軍節度。

translations.literal: The Emperor was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West, bearing credentials, encamped in Guanzhong, as coordinator of the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West with baton and seal, stationed in Guanzhong as overall coordinator of the western armies.

sentences.zh: 淮攻維別將句安於麹，久而不決。

translations.literal: Huai attacked Jiang Wei's separate general Gou An at Qu, long without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai besieged Jiang Wei’s subordinate Gou An at Qu for months without breaking the stalemate.

sentences.zh: 帝乃進據長城，南趣駱谷以疑之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then advanced and occupied Changcheng, south hurrying toward Luogu Valley in order to confuse them.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao pushed forward to Changcheng and feinted south toward Luogu Valley to pull Jiang Wei’s attention.

sentences.zh: 維懼，退保南鄭，安軍絕援，帥眾來降。

translations.literal: Wei feared, withdrew to protect Nanzheng; An's army cut off support; he led the host to come surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei drew back to Nanzheng; Gou An, cut off from help, brought his command over to Wei.

sentences.zh: 轉安東將軍、持節，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East, bearing credentials, garrisoning Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He rotated to General Who Pacifies the East with credentials and took charge at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 及大軍討王淩，帝督淮北諸軍事，帥師會于項。

translations.literal: When the great army punished Wang Ling, the Emperor supervised Huainan north military affairs and led troops to assemble at Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Wang Ling he directed all forces north of the Huai and brought his column to Xiang to join the main host.

sentences.zh: 增邑三百戶，假金印紫綬。

translations.literal: His fief was increased three hundred households; he was lent gold seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: His fief grew by three hundred households and he received the gold seal on purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 尋進號都督，統征東將軍胡遵、鎮東將軍諸葛誕伐吳，戰于東關。

translations.literal: Soon he advanced in title to Area Commander-in-Chief, overall commanding General Who Conquers the East Hu Zun and General Who Guards the East Zhuge Dan to attack Wu, battling at Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he took the area command, leading Hu Zun and Zhuge Dan in an eastern push against Wu that ended at Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 二軍敗績，坐失侯。

translations.literal: The two armies suffered rout; by sitting he lost the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Both columns were routed, and he lost his marquisate for the defeat.

sentences.zh: 蜀將姜維又寇隴右，揚聲欲攻狄道。

translations.literal: Shu general Jiang Wei again raided Longyou, raising sound that he wished to attack Didao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei struck Longyou again, proclaiming that his objective was Didao.

sentences.zh: 以帝行征西將軍，次長安。

translations.literal: They appointed the Emperor acting General Who Conquers the West, halting at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao was given acting rank as General Who Conquers the West and encamped at Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史陳泰欲先賊據狄道，帝曰：「姜維攻羌，收其質任，聚穀作邸閣訖，而復轉行至此，正欲了塞外諸羌，為後年之資耳。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yongzhou Chen Tai wished before the bandits to occupy Didao; the Emperor said: Jiang Wei attacks the Qiang, collects their hostages, gathers grain and finishes building depot-pavilions, then again shifts march to here—just wishing to settle the various Qiang beyond the passes, as resources for later years.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai of Yongzhou wanted to seize Didao first, but Sima Zhao argued that Jiang Wei was busy subduing the Qiang, taking hostages, and filling his granaries and depots, that he swung this way only to finish the frontier tribes and bank supplies for another year, and that he did not mean to storm Didao.

sentences.zh: 若實向狄道，安肯宣露，令外人知？

translations.literal: If he truly were heading toward Didao, how would he be willing to proclaim and expose it, letting outsiders know?
translations.idiomatic: If Didao were really his target, why advertise it to us?

sentences.zh: 今揚聲言出，此欲歸也。

translations.literal: Now raising sound and saying he sets out—this means he wishes to return.
translations.idiomatic: This noise about a march means he is pulling out.

sentences.zh: 」維果燒營而去。

translations.literal: Wei indeed burned the camp and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei torched his camp and withdrew, as Sima Zhao had predicted.

sentences.zh: 會新平羌胡叛，帝擊破之，遂耀兵靈州，北虜震讋，叛者悉降。

translations.literal: When Xinping Qiang and Hu rebelled, the Emperor struck and defeated them; then he displayed troops at Lingzhou; northern captives trembled with fear; rebels all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang and Hu of Xinping rose, he crushed them, paraded his strength at Lingzhou, and terrified the northern tribes until every rebel submitted.

sentences.zh: 以功復封新城鄉侯。

translations.literal: By merit he was again enfeoffed village marquis of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: For that victory he was re-enfeoffed as marquis of Xincheng township.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公之立也，以參定策，進封高都侯，增封二千戶。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang was established, by participating in settling the plan he was advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Gaodu, increase fief two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Because he helped set Cao Mao on the throne, he was promoted to Marquis of Gaodu with two thousand extra households.

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉、文欽之亂，大軍東征，帝兼中領軍，留鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin, the great army east campaigned; the Emperor concurrently held Central Army Supervisor, remaining to garrison Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rose in the east, Sima Zhao stayed in Luoyang as concurrent Central Army Supervisor while the main host marched away.

sentences.zh: 及景帝疾篤，帝自京都省疾，拜衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing's illness was grave, the Emperor himself from the capital visited the illness and was appointed General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Shi lay dying, Sima Zhao hurried from the capital to his bedside and received appointment as General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 景帝崩，天子命帝鎮許昌，尚書傅嘏帥六軍還京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing died, the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor to garrison Xuchang; Director of the Secretariat Fu Gu led the six armies back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Sima Shi’s death the emperor ordered Sima Zhao to hold Xuchang while Fu Gu of the Secretariat brought the six armies back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝用嘏及鐘會策，自帥軍而還。

translations.literal: The Emperor employed Gu's and Zhong Hui's stratagem, himself leading the army and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Heeding Fu Gu and Zhong Hui, he turned his own command about and marched on the capital.

sentences.zh: 至洛陽，進位大將軍加侍中，都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，輔政，劍履上殿。

translations.literal: Arriving at Luoyang, he was advanced in position to Great General, added Palace Attendant, Area Commander-in-Chief of all central command and regional military, recording Director of the Secretariat affairs, assisting government, sword and shoes on the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Luoyang he rose to Great General with concurrent Palace Attendant, overall military command, control of the Secretariat, regency powers, and the right to wear sword and shoes in the throne hall.

sentences.zh: 帝固辭不受。

translations.literal: The Emperor firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined repeatedly and would not take the posts.

sentences.zh: 甘露元年春正月，加大都督，奏事不名。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Ganlu, he was increased to Grand Area Commander-in-Chief; memorializing affairs, not naming himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Ganlu year 1, he was raised to Grand Area Commander-in-Chief and allowed to memorialize without signing his name.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，進封高都公，地方七百里，加之九錫，假斧鉞，進號大都督，劍履上殿。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month, he was advanced to Duke of Gaodu, territory seven hundred li square, added the nine bestowals, lent axe and yue, advanced in title to Grand Commander-in-Chief, sword and shoes on the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer he was made Duke of Gaodu with a domain seven hundred li square, granted the nine insignia and the ritual axes, promoted to Grand Commander-in-Chief, and again allowed sword and shoes in the hall.

sentences.zh: 又固辭不受。

translations.literal: Again he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Again he refused.

sentences.zh: 秋八月庚申，加假黃鉞，增封三縣。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, gengshen, he was additionally lent the yellow battle-axe; fief was increased three counties.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the eighth month of autumn he received the yellow yue and three more counties were added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 二年夏五月辛未，鎮東大將軍諸葛誕殺揚州刺史樂綝，以淮南作亂，遣子靚為質于吳以請救。

translations.literal: In the second year, summer, fifth month, day xinwei, General Who Guards the East Zhuge Dan killed Inspector of Yangzhou Yue Lin, raised rebellion in Huainan, and sent his son Jing as hostage to Wu to request rescue.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the fifth month of summer, the second year, Zhuge Dan, Grand General Who Guards the East, murdered Yangzhou Inspector Yue Lin, rebelled in Huainan, and sent his son Zhuge Jing east as a hostage to beg Wu for troops.

sentences.zh: 議者請速伐之，帝曰：「誕以毌丘儉輕疾傾覆，今必外連吳寇，此為變大而遲。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated requested to punish him speedily; the Emperor said: "Dan, because Guanqiu Jian was swift and perished, now surely will ally with Wu bandits without; this makes the rebellion large yet slow."
translations.idiomatic: Counselors urged a swift strike, but Sima Zhao said, "Zhuge Dan watched Guanqiu Jian rush to ruin; he will league himself with Wu. That makes his revolt broad-based and slow to ripen."

sentences.zh: 吾當與四方同力，以全勝制之。

translations.literal: I ought together with the four quarters exert united strength, by complete victory to control it.
translations.idiomatic: I will muster every quarter of the realm and grind him down with overwhelming force.

sentences.zh: 」乃表曰：「昔黥布叛逆，漢祖親征；

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized saying: "In the past Qing Bu rebelled; Han's ancestor personally campaigned;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized the throne: "When Qing Bu rose against the Han, Gaozu took the field in person;

sentences.zh: 隗囂違戾，光武西伐；

translations.literal: Wei Xiao was recalcitrant; Guangwu campaigned west;
translations.idiomatic: when Wei Xiao defied the court, Guangwu marched west against him;

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝乘輿仍出：皆所以奮揚赫斯，震耀威武也。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Liezu repeatedly went out in the imperial equipage: all were means by which to rouse awesome majesty and display martial might.
translations.idiomatic: and our own Emperor Ming rode out again and again—all to show the majesty of the throne and the edge of Wei arms.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜暫臨戎，使將士得憑天威。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought temporarily to attend the army, causing officers and soldiers to be able to rely on Heaven's majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should join the host for a time, that every soldier may fight under Heaven’s own banner.

sentences.zh: 今諸軍可五十萬，以眾擊寡，蔑不克矣。

translations.literal: Now the various armies can be five hundred thousand; with the many striking the few, none will not be overcome.
translations.idiomatic: We can put half a million in the field; mass against a handful cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 」秋七月，奉天子及皇太后東征，徵兵青、徐、荊、豫，分取關中游軍，皆會淮北。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, escorting the Son of Heaven and the empress dowager east to campaign, conscripting troops in Qing, Xu, Jing, and Yu, dividing and taking Guanzhong roaming troops, all assembling north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he escorted the emperor and the empress dowager east, drafted men from Qing, Xu, Jing, and Yu, peeled mobile units from Guanzhong, and massed the whole host north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 師次於項，假廷尉何楨節，使淮南，宣慰將士，申明逆順，示以誅賞。

translations.literal: The army halted at Xiang; he lent credentials to Commandant of Justice He Zhen, sending him to Huainan to proclaim comfort to officers and soldiers, clarifying rebellion and obedience, showing execution and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Xiang. He lent his baton to Commandant of Justice He Zhen and sent him through Huainan to hearten the troops, spell out loyalty and treason, and publish the price of each.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝進軍丘頭。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the Emperor advanced the army to Qiutou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu he moved his headquarters forward to Qiutou.

sentences.zh: 吳使文欽、唐咨、全端、全懌等三萬餘人來救誕，諸將逆擊，不能禦。

translations.literal: Wu sent Wen Qin, Tang Zi, Quan Duan, Quan Yi, and others, more than thirty thousand, to come rescue Dan; the various generals intercepted and struck but could not withstand.
translations.idiomatic: Wu threw thirty thousand men under Wen Qin, Tang Zi, Quan Duan, and Quan Yi to Zhuge Dan’s relief; Wei’s generals met them but could not hold the line.

sentences.zh: 將軍李廣臨敵不進，泰山太守常時稱疾不出，並斬之以徇。

translations.literal: General Li Guang faced the enemy and did not advance; Grand Administrator of Taishan Chang Shi claimed illness and did not go out; both were beheaded to display.
translations.idiomatic: General Li Guang froze before the enemy; Taishan’s prefect Chang Shi pleaded sickness and stayed in his yamen—both were executed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 八月，吳將硃異帥兵萬餘人，留輜重于都陸，輕兵至黎漿。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Wu general Zhu Yi led troops of more than ten thousand, leaving baggage trains at Dulu, light troops reaching Lijiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wu’s Zhu Yi brought ten thousand men, parked his supply train at Dulu, and pushed light troops up to Lijiang.

sentences.zh: 監軍石苞、袞州刺史州泰禦之，異退。

translations.literal: Army Supervisor Shi Bao and Inspector of Yan Province Zhou Tai opposed them; Yi withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Army Supervisor Shi Bao and Yanzhou Inspector Zhou Tai checked him, and Zhu Yi fell back.

sentences.zh: 泰山太守胡烈以奇兵襲都陸，焚其糧運。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Taishan Hu Lie with odd troops raided Dulu and burned their grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Taishan’s prefect Hu Lie slipped a column to Dulu, torched Zhu Yi’s grain carts, and cut his supply line.

sentences.zh: 苞、泰復進擊異，大破之。

translations.literal: Bao and Tai again advanced and struck Yi, greatly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao and Zhou Tai pressed the attack and shattered Zhu Yi’s command.

sentences.zh: 異之餘卒餒甚，食葛葉而遁，吳人殺異。

translations.literal: Yi's remaining soldiers were extremely hungry; they ate kudzu leaves and fled; Wu men killed Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His survivors starved until they chewed kudzu leaves on the retreat; Wu’s court then executed Zhu Yi for the defeat.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「異不得至壽春，非其罪也，而吳人殺之，適以謝壽春而堅誕意，使其猶望救耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Yi not being able to reach Shouchun was not his crime, yet Wu men killed him—just right to apologize to Shouchun and harden Dan's resolve, causing him still to hope for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao observed that Zhu Yi never reached Shouchun through no fault of his own, yet Wu executed him—an offering to placate Shouchun that only steels Zhuge Dan’s hope of relief.

sentences.zh: 若其不爾，彼當突圍，決一旦之命。

translations.literal: If it is not thus, they ought to break the encirclement and decide a single dawn's fate.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they would have tried to cut their way out and hazard everything on one dawn.

sentences.zh: 或謂大軍不能久，省食減口，冀有他變。

translations.literal: Some say the great army cannot long endure, economizing food and reducing mouths, hoping there will be other changes.
translations.idiomatic: Some think we cannot keep this siege and ration their food and ours, waiting for fortune to turn.

sentences.zh: 料賊之情，不出此三者。

translations.literal: Estimating the bandits' disposition, it does not go beyond these three kinds.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy’s mind will move along one of those three tracks—no more.

sentences.zh: 今當多方以亂之，備其越逸，此勝計也。

translations.literal: Now one ought by many means to disorder them, guard against their leaping escape—this is the plan of victory.
translations.idiomatic: We should confuse them on every front and block any breakout—that is how we win.

sentences.zh: 」因命合圍，分遣羸疾就穀淮北，稟軍士大豆，人三升。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered closing the siege, separately sending weak and sick to obtain grain north of the Huai, issuing soldiers soybeans, three sheng per person.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the ring closed, sent the sick and feeble to draw grain north of the Huai, and issued each soldier three sheng of beans.

sentences.zh: 欽聞之，果喜。

translations.literal: When Qin heard it, he indeed rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin heard the news and crowed with delight.

sentences.zh: 帝愈羸形以示之，多縱反間，揚言吳救方至。

translations.literal: The Emperor further showed them emaciated form, widely set loose counter-espionage, publicly declaring Wu rescue was about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao played up his army’s hunger, sowed a net of false rumors, and let word spread that Wu’s relief fleet was almost here.

sentences.zh: 誕等益寬恣食，俄而城中乏糧。

translations.literal: Dan and the others increasingly relaxed and ate at will; soon the city within lacked grain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan’s men relaxed and ate their stores freely—then suddenly the granaries inside the walls ran dry.

sentences.zh: 石苞、王基並請攻之，帝曰：「誕之逆謀，非一朝一夕也，聚糧完守，外結吳人，自謂足據淮南。

translations.literal: Shi Bao and Wang Ji together requested to attack him; the Emperor said: "Dan's treasonous plot is not one morning and one evening; he gathered grain and completed defense, outwardly allied with Wu men, himself deeming it sufficient to occupy Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao and Wang Ji begged leave to storm the walls, but Sima Zhao said, "Zhuge Dan did not hatch this plot overnight; he stocked grain, shored his defenses, and leagued with Wu because he believed he could hold the Huai basin."

sentences.zh: 欽既同惡相濟，必不便走。

translations.literal: Qin, having joined evils and aided each other, surely is not convenient to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qin is tied to him in guilt; neither will slip away easily.

sentences.zh: 今若急攻之，損遊軍之力。

translations.literal: Now if one urgently attacks them, it injures roaming army strength.
translations.idiomatic: A hasty assault would only waste our mobile columns.

sentences.zh: 外寇卒至，表裏受敵，此危道也。

translations.literal: Outer bandits suddenly arrive; inside and outside receive enemy—this is a perilous way.
translations.idiomatic: If Wu struck while we were entangled, we would be caught front and rear—that is the road to disaster.

sentences.zh: 今三叛相聚於孤城之中，天其或者將使同戮。

translations.literal: Now the three rebels gather together within a lone city; Heaven perhaps will cause them to be slain together.
translations.idiomatic: The three traitors are bottled in one town; Heaven may mean to destroy them in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 吾當以長策縻之，但堅守三面。

translations.literal: I ought by long stratagem to tether them, only firmly guarding three sides.
translations.idiomatic: I will leash them with patience and seal three faces of the walls.

sentences.zh: 若賊陸道而來，軍糧必少，吾以遊兵輕騎絕其轉輸，可不戰而破外賊。

translations.literal: If the bandits come by land route, army grain must be few; I with roaming troops and light cavalry cut off their transport, can without battle break the outer bandits.
