translations.idiomatic: If they march overland their baggage train will be thin; our flying columns can sever it and break the relief host without a pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 外賊破，欽等必成擒矣。

translations.literal: When outer bandits are broken, Qin and others must be completed captures.
translations.idiomatic: Break the relief army and Wen Qin is ours for the taking.

sentences.zh: 」全懌母，孫權女也，得罪于吳，全端兄子禕及儀奉其母來奔。

translations.literal: Quan Yi's mother was Sun Quan's daughter; she offended in Wu; Quan Duan's elder brother's sons led her mother coming to flee hither.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi’s mother was a daughter of Sun Quan; out of favor in Wu, she was escorted to the Wei lines by two nephews of Quan Duan.

sentences.zh: 儀兄靜時在壽春，用鐘會計，作禕、儀書以譎靜。

translations.literal: Yi's elder brother Jing was at that time in Shouchun; employing Zhong Hui's plan, they forged letters in the names of the defectors in order to deceive Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jing was still in Shouchun with Zhuge Dan; Zhong Hui forged letters in the names of the defectors to bait him.

sentences.zh: 靜兄弟五人帥其眾來降，城中大駭。

translations.literal: Jing and brothers five persons led their host to come surrender; within the city there was great terror.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jing and four brothers brought their followers over the wall, and panic swept the city.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月壬寅，誕、欽等出攻長圍，諸軍逆擊，走之。

translations.literal: Third year, spring, first month, day renyin, Dan, Qin, and others went out to attack the long siege lines; the various armies intercepted and struck, routing them.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin in the first month of spring, the third year, Zhuge Dan and Wen Qin sallied against the outer stockade; Wei’s lines threw them back in disorder.

sentences.zh: 初，誕、欽內不相協，及至窮蹙，轉相疑貳。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Dan and Qin inwardly were not harmonious; when it came to extreme distress, they turned to mutual suspicion and divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Dan and Qin had never trusted each other; under the press of the siege their alliance curdled into mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 會欽計事與誕忤，誕手刃殺欽。

translations.literal: When they met to plan affairs Qin contradicted Dan; Dan with his own hand blade killed Qin.
translations.idiomatic: At a council Wen Qin crossed Zhuge Dan, who drew his sword and cut him down on the spot.

sentences.zh: 欽子鴦攻誕，不克，逾城降。

translations.literal: Qin's son Yang attacked Dan, did not overcome, crossed the wall and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yang struck at Dan, failed, and climbed the wall to surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 以為將軍，封侯，使鴦巡城而呼。

translations.literal: He was made a general, enfeoffed marquis, and caused Yang to patrol the wall and shout.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao named him a general and a marquis and sent him along the parapet to shout defiance at the defenders.

sentences.zh: 帝見城上持弓者不發，謂諸將曰：「可攻矣！

translations.literal: The Emperor saw those on the wall holding bows did not shoot; he said to the various generals: "It can be attacked!
translations.idiomatic: When he saw the archers on the battlements stand idle, he told his generals the moment had come to storm the walls!

sentences.zh: 」二月乙酉，攻而拔之，斬誕，夷三族。

translations.literal: Second month, day yiyou, attacked and took it, beheaded Dan, exterminated three clans.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the second month the city fell; Zhuge Dan was executed and his kin to the third degree extirpated.

sentences.zh: 吳將唐咨、孫彌、徐韶等帥其屬皆降，表加爵位，稟其餒疾。

translations.literal: Wu generals Tang Zi, Sun Mi, Xu Shao, and others led their subordinates all to surrender; he memorialized to add noble ranks and issued their hungry and sick.
translations.idiomatic: Wu’s Tang Zi, Sun Mi, Xu Shao, and their commands yielded; Sima Zhao memorialized for titles for them and saw to the hungry and wounded.

sentences.zh: 或言吳兵必不為用，請坑之。

translations.literal: Some said Wu troops surely would not be usable; requested to pit them.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged that Wu soldiers could never be trusted and should be buried alive.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「就令亡還，適見中國之弘耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Even letting them flee back, just then shows the Central State's magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao replied that even if they drifted home to Wu, it would only advertise the breadth of the Middle Kingdom’s mercy.

sentences.zh: 」於是徙之三河。

translations.literal: Thereupon relocated them to the Three Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled them in the Three Rivers region instead.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，歸於京師，魏帝命改丘頭曰武丘，以旌武功。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, returned to the capital; the Wei emperor ordered to change Qiutou to Wuqiu, in order to display martial merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he returned to Luoyang, and the Wei emperor renamed Qiutou as Wuqiu to commemorate the victory.

sentences.zh: 五月，天子以并州之太原上党西河樂平新興雁門、司州之河東平陽八郡，地方七百里，封帝為晉公，加九錫，進位相國，晉國置官司焉。

translations.literal: Fifth month, the Son of Heaven with Bingzhou's Taiyuan, Shangdang, Xihe, Leping, Xinxing, Yanmen, and Sizhou's Hedong, Pingyang—eight commanderies, territory seven hundred li square—enfeoffed the Emperor as Duke of Jin, added the nine bestowals, advanced position to Chancellor of State, and the Jin state set up offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor granted Sima Zhao eight commanderies—six from Bingzhou plus Hedong and Pingyang from Sizhou—seven hundred li square, raised him to Duke of Jin with the nine gifts and the chancellorship, and authorized a full Jin administration.

sentences.zh: 九讓，乃止。

translations.literal: Nine times he declined; then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He demurred nine times before the offer was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 於是增邑萬戶，食三縣，諸子之無爵者皆封列侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon increased fief by ten thousand households, eating three counties; sons without noble rank were all enfeoffed full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: As consolation his fief rose by ten thousand households across three counties, and every son without a title was made a full marquis.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，奏錄先世名臣元功大勳之子了，隨才敘用。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, memorialized to record and employ the sons of former generations' famous ministers and of those who rendered founding merit and great service, according to talent arranging appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he memorialized to enroll the sons of past worthies and of families that had earned great merit at the founding, and to place them according to ability.

sentences.zh: 四年夏六月，分荊州置二都督，王基鎮新野，州泰鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Fourth year, summer, sixth month, divided Jingzhou and set up two area commands; Wang Ji garrisoned Xinye, Zhou Ta garrisoned Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer, the fourth year, Jingzhou was split into two commands: Wang Ji took Xinye and Zhou Ta took Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 使石苞都督揚州，陳騫都督豫州，鐘毓都督徐州，宋鈞監青州諸軍事。

translations.literal: He made Shi Bao area commander of Yangzhou, Chen Qian area commander of Yuzhou, Zhong Yu area commander of Xuzhou, Song Jun supervised Qingzhou military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He named Shi Bao over Yangzhou, Chen Qian over Yuzhou, Zhong Yu over Xuzhou, and Song Jun to oversee Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 景元元年夏四月，天子復命帝爵秩如前，又讓不受。

translations.literal: First year of Jingyuan, summer, fourth month, the Son of Heaven again ordered the Emperor noble rank and emolument as before; again he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Jingyuan year 1, the emperor repeated the old offer of rank and stipend; Sima Zhao refused once more.

sentences.zh: 天子既以帝三世宰輔，政非己出，情不能安，又慮廢辱，將臨軒召百僚而行放黜。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, because the Emperor for three generations was chief minister, government was not of himself issuing, inwardly could not be at peace, also feared deposition and humiliation, was about to ascend the gallery and summon the hundred officials and carry out dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mao saw three generations of Simas hold the real power; unable to bear a throne that was hollow, and fearing deposition, he prepared to call the high ministers to the front hall and strike first.

sentences.zh: 五月戊子夜，使冗從僕射李昭等發甲於陵雲台，召侍中王沈、散騎常侍王業、尚書王經，出懷中黃素詔示之，戒嚴俟旦。

translations.literal: Fifth month, night of wuzi, he ordered Supernumerary Household Coachman Li Zhao and others to raise armor at Lingyun Terrace, summoned Palace Attendant Wang Chen, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Ye, Director Wang Jing, produced from his bosom the yellow plain edict and showed them, martial law awaiting dawn.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of wuzi in the fifth month he had Li Zhao and others arm the guards at Lingyun Terrace, summoned Wang Chen, Wang Ye, and Director Wang Jing, drew a yellow silk edict from his breast, showed it to them, and ordered martial law until dawn.

sentences.zh: 沈、業馳告於帝，帝召護軍賈充等為之備。

translations.literal: Chen and Ye galloped to inform the Emperor; the Emperor summoned Army Protector Jia Chong and others to prepare for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen and Wang Ye galloped to Sima Zhao with the news; he called Jia Chong and other guards to readiness.

sentences.zh: 天子知事泄，帥左右攻相府，稱有所討，敢有動者族誅。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven knew the affair had leaked; leading those at his left and right he attacked the chancellor's mansion, declaring there was something to punish; whoever dared move—clan execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Mao saw the plot had leaked, he led his attendants against the chancellor’s palace, shouting a punitive purpose and threatening clan extinction on anyone who stirred.

sentences.zh: 相府兵將止不敢戰，賈充叱諸將曰：「公畜養汝輩，正為今日耳！

translations.literal: Chancellor mansion soldiers and generals stopped and did not dare fight; Jia Chong shouted at the various generals: "The lord raised and nurtured you lot—just for this day!
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor’s guards hung back until Jia Chong roared at them that the regent had fed them all these years for exactly this hour!

sentences.zh: 」太子舍人成濟抽戈犯蹕，刺之，刃出於背，天子崩于車中。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Household Attendant Cheng Ji drew spear and violated the imperial progress, stabbed him; the blade came out his back; the Son of Heaven died in the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ji, a cadet of the heir apparent’s household, drove his spear through the imperial train; the blade passed clean through Cao Mao’s back, and the emperor died in his chariot.

sentences.zh: 帝召百僚謀其故，僕射陳泰不至。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned the hundred officials to deliberate the reason; Vice Director Chen Tai did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao assembled the ministers to account for the killing, but Vice Director Chen Tai stayed away.

sentences.zh: 帝遣其舅荀顗輿致之，延于曲室，謂曰：「玄伯，天下其如我何？

translations.literal: The Emperor sent his maternal uncle Xun Yi in a litter to bring him, extended him in a side chamber, saying: "Xuanbo, what will all under Heaven do to me?
translations.idiomatic: He sent his uncle Xun Yi in a litter to fetch Chen Tai into a side room and asked, "Xuanbo, what is the realm going to say of me now?"

sentences.zh: 」泰曰：「惟腰斬賈充，微以謝天下。

translations.literal: Tai said: "Only to waist-cut Jia Chong, slightly thereby to apologize to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai answered, "Only cutting Jia Chong in two at the waist would begin to appease the empire."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿更思其次。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You further think of the next.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao said, "Think of something short of that."

sentences.zh: 」泰曰：「但見其上。

translations.literal: Tai said: "Only see what is above.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai said he saw nothing beyond that measure.

sentences.zh: 不見其次。

translations.literal: Do not see what is next.
translations.idiomatic: He could not name a lesser remedy.

sentences.zh: 」於是歸罪成濟而斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon attributed guilt to Cheng Ji and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao pinned the deed on Cheng Ji and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 太后令曰：「昔漢昌邑王以罪發為庶人，此兒亦宜以庶人禮葬之，使外內咸知其所行也。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered saying: "In the past Han's King of Changyi by crime was dismissed as commoner; this child also ought to be buried by commoner rites, causing outer and inner all to know what he did.
translations.idiomatic: The Dowager issued an order that when Han deposed the king of Changyi, he was buried as a commoner, and that this boy should be buried likewise, that court and countryside might know his crimes.

sentences.zh: 」殺尚書王經，貳於我也。

translations.literal: Kill Director Wang Jing—he was double toward me.
translations.idiomatic: Execute Director Wang Jing for disloyalty to me.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，帝奏曰：「故高貴鄉公帥從駕人兵，拔刃鳴鼓向臣所，臣懼兵刃相接，即敕將士不得有所傷害，違令者以軍法從事。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the Emperor memorialized saying: "The former Duke of Gaoguixiang led attendant-follower men-at-arms, drew blades and beat drums toward your subject's place; your subject feared weapons clashing, immediately ordered officers and soldiers not to permit any harm; those who violated the order were by military law dealt with.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Sima Zhao memorialized that the late Duke of Gaoguixiang had led his escort with naked blades and beating drums against the chancellor’s residence; fearing a melee, he had ordered his men not to harm the sovereign and had threatened military law on anyone who disobeyed.

sentences.zh: 騎督成倅弟太子舍人濟入兵陣，傷公至隕。

translations.literal: Cavalry Supervisor Cheng Cui's younger brother, Crown Prince Household Attendant Ji, entered the battle array, wounded the duke unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry inspector Cheng Cui’s brother Cheng Ji, a cadet of the heir’s household, plunged into the ranks and mortally wounded the duke.

sentences.zh: 臣聞人臣之節，有死無貳，事上之義，不敢逃難。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the integrity of a human minister is: there is death, no double loyalty; the righteousness of serving superiors: dare not flee hardship.
translations.idiomatic: A minister owes single-minded loyalty unto death and must not shrink from danger in serving his lord.

sentences.zh: 前者變故卒至，禍同發機，誠欲委身守死，惟命所裁。

translations.literal: The former sudden change arrived as if calamity together loosed a trigger; truly wishing to cast away body and guard death, only as fate decrees cut.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis struck like a sprung trap, I was ready to lay down my life and await Heaven’s verdict.

sentences.zh: 然惟本謀，乃欲上危皇太后，傾覆宗廟。

translations.literal: Yet as for the root plot, then he wished above to endanger the empress dowager, overturn the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the plot itself aimed to threaten the empress dowager and overturn the dynastic shrines.

sentences.zh: 臣忝當元輔，義在安國，即駱驛申敕，不得迫近輿輦。

translations.literal: Your subject shamefully occupies chief minister; righteousness lies in pacifying the state; immediately repeatedly issued orders not to press near the imperial carriages.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister my duty was to steady the state; I sent order after order that no one press the imperial carriages.

sentences.zh: 而濟妄入陣間，以致大變，哀怛痛恨，五內摧裂。

translations.literal: Yet Ji rashly entered amid the array, thereby causing the great change; grief and pain, hatred and regret, the five viscera tear apart.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ji broke into the ranks on his own and brought on catastrophe; my grief and rage tear me apart within.

sentences.zh: 濟幹國亂紀，罪不容誅，輒收濟家屬，付廷尉。

translations.literal: Ji interfered with the state and disordered the statutes; his guilt exceeds what execution can exhaust—immediately seized Ji's family dependents, handed to Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ji disturbed the state and broke every law; his crime exceeds death itself—I have seized his kin and remanded them to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 」太后從之，夷濟三族。

translations.literal: The empress dowager followed it; exterminated Ji's three clans.
translations.idiomatic: The Dowager approved, and Cheng Ji’s kin to the third degree were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 與公卿議，立燕王宇之子常道鄉公璜為帝。

translations.literal: Together with dukes and ministers he deliberated, establishing Prince of Yan Yu's son, Duke of Changdaoxiang Huang, as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: With the high ministers he agreed to set Cao Huang, the Duke of Changdaoxiang and son of Prince Yu of Yan, on the throne.

sentences.zh: 六月，改元。

translations.literal: Sixth month, changed era name.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，天子進帝為相國，封晉公，增十郡，加九錫如初，群從子弟未侯者封亭侯，賜錢千萬，帛萬匹。

translations.literal: On bingchen, the Son of Heaven advanced the Emperor to Chancellor of State, enfeoffed Duke of Jin, increased ten commanderies, added the nine bestowals as at first; group follow younger kin not yet marquis were enfeoffed village marquis; bestowed ten million cash, ten thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the emperor named Sima Zhao chancellor and Duke of Jin, added ten commanderies, renewed the nine gifts, made every cousin and nephew not yet titled a village marquis, and granted ten million cash and ten thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 固讓，乃止。

translations.literal: Firmly declined; then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He declined until the court let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，吳吉陽督蕭慎以書詣鎮東將軍石苞偽降，求迎。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, Wu Jiyang Supervisor Xiao Shen with a letter went to General Who Guards the East Shi Bao feigning surrender, requesting to be welcomed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh winter month Wu’s Jiyang garrison commander Xiao Shen wrote to Shi Bao pretending to defect and asking for an escort.

sentences.zh: 帝知其詐也，使苞外示迎之，而內為之備。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew it was deceit; he ordered Bao outwardly to show welcoming them, while inwardly to prepare for it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao saw the ruse and told Shi Bao to feign acceptance while laying a trap within.

sentences.zh: 二年秋八月甲寅，天子使太尉高柔授帝相國印綬，司空鄭沖致晉公茅土九錫，固辭。

translations.literal: Second year, autumn, eighth month, day jiayin, the Son of Heaven sent Grand Commandant Gao Rou to confer on the Emperor the chancellor's seal and ribbon, Minister of Works Zheng Chong to deliver the Duke of Jin fief-soil and nine bestowals; firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the eighth month of autumn, the second year, Gao Rou brought the chancellor’s seal and Zheng Chong the fief-map and nine gifts; Sima Zhao refused them again.

sentences.zh: 三年夏四月，肅慎來獻楛矢、石砮、弓甲、貂皮等，天子命歸於大將軍府。

translations.literal: Third year, summer, fourth month, Sushen came to present birch arrows, stone arrowheads, bows, armor, sable pelts, and the like; the Son of Heaven ordered them returned to the Great General's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, the third year, Sushen envoys brought birch arrows, stone heads, arms, and sable skins; the emperor directed the tribute to the grand general’s residence.

sentences.zh: 四年春二月丁丑，天子復命帝如前，又固讓。

translations.literal: Fourth year, spring, second month, day dingchou, the Son of Heaven again ordered the Emperor as before; again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou in the second month of spring, the fourth year, the emperor repeated the old honors; Sima Zhao refused again.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔大將軍府增置司馬一人，從事中郎二人，舍人十人。

translations.literal: Third month, edict: Great General's mansion additionally establish one Major, two Retainers, ten Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month an edict added one major, two retainers, and ten gentlemen to the grand general’s staff.

sentences.zh: 夏，帝將伐蜀，乃謀眾曰：「自定壽春已來，息役六年，治兵繕甲，以擬二虜。

translations.literal: Summer, the Emperor was about to campaign against Shu; then he consulted the host saying: "Since settling Shouchun, we have rested corvée six years, drilled troops and repaired armor, in order to target the two bandits.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, as he readied the Shu expedition, he told his council, "Six years have passed since Shouchun fell—six years we have spent forging arms to meet Wu and Shu."

sentences.zh: 略計取吳，作戰船，通水道，當用千餘萬功，此十萬人百數十日事也。

translations.literal: Roughly calculating taking Wu, building war boats, opening water routes, ought to use more than ten million man-days of work; this is a matter of one hundred several tens of days for one hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: A Wu campaign—building hulls and dredging channels—would swallow ten million man-days; a hundred thousand laborers would need months on end.

sentences.zh: 又南土下濕，必生疾疫。

translations.literal: Moreover southern soil is low and damp; surely sickness and pestilence will arise.
translations.idiomatic: The southern marshes breed sickness; an army would wilt there.

sentences.zh: 今宜先取蜀，三年之後，在巴蜀順流之勢，水陸並進，此滅虞定虢，吞韓並魏之勢也。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting first to take Shu; after three years, with Ba-Shu's down-current momentum, water and land advancing together—this is the momentum of destroying Yu and settling Guo, swallowing Han and annexing Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Better to take Shu first; three years later, riding the Yangzi current from Ba and Shu, we can move by water and land together—the old stratagem of swallowing the neighbor to fatten the conqueror.

sentences.zh: 計蜀戰士九萬，居守成都及備他郡不下四萬，然則餘眾不過五萬。

translations.literal: Calculating Shu warriors ninety thousand; dwelling to guard Chengdu and garrison other commanderies not less than forty thousand; then the remaining host does not exceed fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shu lists ninety thousand troops, but forty thousand must hold Chengdu and the outlying commanderies—no more than fifty thousand can meet us in the field.

sentences.zh: 今絆姜維於遝中，使不得東顧，直指駱穀，出其空虛之地，以襲漢中。

translations.literal: Now pin Jiang Wei in Taozhong, causing him not to be able to look east; point straight to Luogu Valley, emerge in their empty hollow ground, to raid Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Pin Jiang Wei in Taozhong so he cannot shift east, then drive straight through Luogu into the empty heart of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 彼若嬰城守險，兵勢必散，首尾離絕。

translations.literal: If they gird the city and guard the peril, military momentum must scatter; head and tail are cut off.
translations.idiomatic: If they hug the walls and cling to the defiles, their strength will splinter and van detach from van.

sentences.zh: 舉大眾以屠城，散銳卒以略野，劍閣不暇守險，關頭不能自存。

translations.literal: Raise a great host to slaughter the city; scatter picked troops to sweep the wilds; Jiange will have no leisure to guard the peril; Guantou cannot preserve itself.
translations.idiomatic: Mass the army to storm the towns, send flying columns to scour the open country, and Jiange will have no time to hold the narrows while the Guan passes collapse on their own.

sentences.zh: 以劉禪之暗，而邊城外破，士女內震，其亡可知也。

translations.literal: With Liu Shan's darkness, and border cities broken from without, gentlemen and ladies within shaken, its perishing can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan is a dull tool; once the frontier cracks and panic seizes the capital, his fall is a foregone conclusion.

sentences.zh: 」征西將軍鄧艾以為未有釁，屢陳異議。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West Deng Ai thought there was not yet a crack, repeatedly presented divergent opinions.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai, the western commander, argued there was no opening yet and kept filing objections.

sentences.zh: 帝患之，使主簿師纂為艾司馬以喻之，艾乃奉命。

translations.literal: The Emperor worried about it, ordered Chief Clerk Shi Zuan to become Ai's Major in order to instruct him; Ai then received the command.
translations.idiomatic: Annoyed by Deng Ai’s foot-dragging, Sima Zhao made his chief clerk Shi Zuan Deng’s deputy to talk sense into him; Deng then accepted the order.

sentences.zh: 於是征四方之兵十八萬，使鄧艾自狄道攻姜維於遝中，雍州刺史諸葛緒自祁山軍于武街，絕維歸路，鎮西將軍鐘會帥前將軍李輔、征蜀護軍胡烈等自駱穀襲漢中。

translations.literal: Thereupon conscripted troops of the four quarters one hundred eighty thousand, ordered Deng Ai from Didao to attack Jiang Wei in Taozhong, Inspector of Yongzhou Zhuge Xu from Qishan to encamp at Wujie, cutting off Jiang Wei's return route, General Who Guards the West Zhong Hui leading Former General Li Fu, Shu Campaign Protector Hu Lie, and others from Luogu Valley to raid Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a hundred and eighty thousand men from every quarter: Deng Ai moved from Didao against Jiang Wei in Taozhong; Yongzhou Inspector Zhuge Xu marched from Qishan to Wujie to sever Jiang Wei’s retreat; Zhong Hui, General Who Guards the West, led Li Fu, Hu Lie, and the rest through Luogu against Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，軍發洛陽，大賚將士，陳師誓眾。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, the army set out from Luoyang, greatly rewarded officers and soldiers, arrayed the host and swore the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn the host left Luoyang after rich gifts to the ranks, a full review, and oaths to the army.

sentences.zh: 將軍鄧敦謂蜀未可討，帝斬以徇。

translations.literal: General Deng Dun said Shu could not be punished; the Emperor beheaded him to display.
translations.idiomatic: General Deng Dun said Shu was not ripe for attack; Sima Zhao struck off his head as a warning.

sentences.zh: 九月，又使天水太守王頎攻維營，隴西太守牽弘邀其前，金城太守楊頎趣甘松。

translations.literal: Ninth month, again ordered Tianshui Grand Administrator Wang Qi to attack Wei's camp, Longxi Grand Administrator Qian Hong to intercept his front, Jincheng Grand Administrator Yang Qi to hurry to Gansong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he sent Tianshui’s Wang Qi against Jiang Wei’s camp, Longxi’s Qian Hong to block his van, and Jincheng’s Yang Qi toward Gansong.

sentences.zh: 鐘會分為二隊，入自斜谷，使李輔圍王含于樂城，又使步將易愷攻蔣斌于漢城。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui divided into two columns, entered from Xie Valley, ordered Li Fu to besiege Wang Han at Lecheng, also ordered infantry general Yi Kai to attack Jiang Bin at Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui split his force, entered by Xie Valley, set Li Fu to invest Wang Han at Lecheng, and sent Yi Kai against Jiang Bin at Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 會直指陽安，護軍胡烈攻陷關城。

translations.literal: Hui pointed straight to Yang'an; Protector Hu Lie attacked and took Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui drove straight on Yang’an while Protector Hu Lie stormed the pass fort.

sentences.zh: 姜維聞之，引還，王頎追敗維于強川。

translations.literal: When Jiang Wei heard it, he led back; Wang Qi pursued and defeated Wei at Qiangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei wheeled about; Wang Qi ran him down at Qiangchuan and broke his column.

sentences.zh: 維與張翼、廖化合軍守劍閣，鐘會攻之。

translations.literal: Wei joined Zhang Yi and Liao Hua combining armies to guard Jiange; Zhong Hui attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei joined Zhang Yi and Liao Hua to hold Jiange; Zhong Hui laid siege.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，天子以諸侯獻捷交至，乃申前命曰：

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, the Son of Heaven because the nobles' presented victories arrived in succession, then reiterated the former command saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month, as victory dispatches from the lords piled in, the emperor renewed his earlier charge, saying:

sentences.zh: 朕以寡德，獲承天序，嗣我祖宗之洪烈。

translations.literal: We, with scant virtue, have obtained to inherit Heaven's ordering, continuing our ancestors' and forebears' vast blazing merit.
translations.idiomatic: We, though lacking in virtue, have received the Mandate and carry forward the great enterprise of our forebears.

sentences.zh: 遭家多難，不明於訓。

translations.literal: Encountering the house's many hardships, not clear in instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The house has suffered repeated trials, and We have not been equal to the lessons of rule.

sentences.zh: 曩者奸逆屢興，方寇內侮，大懼淪喪四海，以墮三祖之弘業。

translations.literal: Formerly traitors and rebels repeatedly arose, border bandits inwardly insulted; greatly fearing the loss and ruin of the four seas, thereby toppling the three ancestors' grand enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Traitors rose again and again while enemies pressed inward; We feared the realm would slip away and the magnificent work of the three founders come to nothing.

sentences.zh: 惟公經德履哲，明允廣深，迪宣武文，世作保傅，以輔乂皇家。

translations.literal: Only you thread virtue and tread wisdom, are enlightened, trustworthy, broad and deep; you enlighten and spread martial and civil; generation after generation you serve as protector and tutor, thereby assisting and governing the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: You embody virtue and wisdom, clear-sighted and steadfast, carrying forward the civil and martial legacy; generation on generation your house has been tutor and bulwark to the throne.

sentences.zh: 櫛風沐雨，周旋征伐，劬勞王室，二十有餘載。

translations.literal: Combing wind and bathing rain, turning in campaigns and punishments, toiling for the royal house, more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Through wind and rain you have marched and fought for the royal house more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 毗翼前人，乃斷大政，克厭不端，維安社稷。

translations.literal: Assisting wing the former men, then you judged great government, were able to quell what was not upright, tied and secured the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: You stood beside Our predecessors, settled the great affairs of state, crushed every irregularity, and steadied the altars.

sentences.zh: 暨儉、欽之亂，公綏援有眾，分命興師，統紀有方，用緝寧淮浦。

translations.literal: When it came to Jian and Qin's rebellion, you pacified and aided the hosts, separately ordered raising armies, ordering statutes had method, thereby used to bring peace to the Huai shores.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rose, you calmed the armies, issued orders to march, kept discipline, and brought quiet again to the banks of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 其後巴蜀屢侵，西土不靖，公奇畫指授，制勝千里。

translations.literal: Afterward Ba-Shu repeatedly encroached, the western land was not quiet; you with marvelous plans pointed and instructed, controlled victory a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: When Ba and Shu raided again and again and the west would not stay still, your stratagems directed the hosts and won victories a thousand leagues away.

sentences.zh: 是以段谷之戰，乘釁大捷，斬將搴旗，效首萬計。

translations.literal: Therefore in the battle of Duangu, riding the crack you achieved a great victory, beheading generals and seizing banners, presenting heads by the ten thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Hence at Duangu you seized the opening, won a crushing victory, struck down generals and hauled off their banners, and piled counted heads by the myriad.

sentences.zh: 孫峻猾夏，致寇徐方，戎車首路，威靈先邁，黃鉞未啟，鯨鯢竄跡。

translations.literal: Sun Jun injured the central states, bringing bandits to Xu region; war chariots took the road first, awesome numen advanced first; the yellow battle-axe not yet opened, whales and calves fled their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jun troubled the heartland and raided Xu province, your host moved first and dread went before it; the golden yue had not yet been raised and the great beasts of Wu were already in flight.

sentences.zh: 孫壹構隙，自相疑阻，幽鑒遠照，奇策洞微，遠人歸命，作籓南夏，爰授銳卒，畢力戎行。

translations.literal: Sun Yi built a rift, mutually suspecting and blocking; your dark mirror shone far, marvelous stratagems penetrated the subtle; distant men submitted their mandate, became fief at southern Xia; then you gave picked troops, exhausted strength on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Yi’s faction turned on itself in mutual suspicion, your far-sighted plans split their counsels; distant peoples pledged allegiance and became a screen for the south, and you armed picked columns to finish the work in the field.

sentences.zh: 暨諸葛誕，滔天作逆，稱兵揚楚，欽、咨逋罪，同惡相濟，帥其蝥賊，以入壽春，憑阻淮山，敢距王命。

translations.literal: When it came to Zhuge Dan, he filled Heaven with rebellion, raised arms in Yang and Chu; Qin, Zi fled their crimes, joined evils aiding each other, led their mantis-bandits, thereby entering Shouchun, relying on Huai mountains' barrier, dared resist the king's command.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhuge Dan rose in monstrous revolt, called arms along the Yangzi and Huai, drew Wen Qin and Tang Zi into his guilt, marched his rabble into Shouchun, and behind the Huai ranges defied the royal command.

sentences.zh: 公躬擐甲胄，龔行在罰，玄謀廟算，遵養時晦。

translations.literal: You personally donned helmet and armor, reverently marched in punishment; dark plans and temple calculations, followed and nurtured the season's obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: You girded on mail yourself and led the punitive host; deep counsel from the temple and patience while Heaven’s hour was still dark.

sentences.zh: 奇兵震擊，而硃異摧破；

translations.literal: Odd troops quaking strike, and Zhu Yi was crushed and broken;
translations.idiomatic: A sudden blow shattered Zhu Yi’s army;

sentences.zh: 神變應機，而全琮稽服；

translations.literal: Spirit change responding to the moment, and Quan Cong bowed in submission;
translations.idiomatic: timely shifts of plan brought Quan Cong to humble submission;

sentences.zh: 取亂攻昧，而高墉不守。

translations.literal: Taking disorder and attacking darkness, and the high walls did not hold.
translations.idiomatic: you struck a foe in chaos and twilight until his high walls could not stand.

sentences.zh: 兼九伐之弘略，究五兵之正度，用能戰不窮武，而大敵殲潰；

translations.literal: Combining the nine punishments' grand strategy, exhausting the five weapons' correct measure, thereby able to fight without exhausting martial force, while the great enemy was annihilated and routed;
translations.idiomatic: You wielded the grand strategy of the nine campaigns and the full measure of the five arms, so that battle did not drain the army yet the great foe was wiped out;

sentences.zh: 旗不再麾，而元憝授首。

translations.literal: The banner did not wave twice, while the chief villain delivered his head.
translations.idiomatic: the standard scarcely had to wave again before the arch-traitor lost his head.

sentences.zh: 收勍吳之雋臣，系亡命之逋虜。

translations.literal: Collected Wu's stalwart ministers, bound fugitive fleeing captives.
translations.idiomatic: You took Wu’s able ministers captive and roped up every runaway.

sentences.zh: 交臂屈膝，委命下吏，俘馘十萬積屍成京。

translations.literal: Crossing arms and bending knees, casting mandate to inferior clerks; captives and severed ears one hundred thousand, piled corpses formed a mound.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed arms, bent the knee, and threw themselves on your mercy; the slain and captive ran past a hundred thousand until corpses heaped like a hill.

sentences.zh: 雪宗廟之滯恥，拯兆庶之艱難。

translations.literal: Wiped the ancestral temple's stagnant shame, rescued the hundred million commoners' hardship and peril.
translations.idiomatic: You washed away the lingering shame of the shrines and lifted the people out of mortal danger.

sentences.zh: 掃平區域，信威吳會，遂戢干戈，靖我疆土，天地鬼神，罔不獲乂。

translations.literal: Swept and leveled the regions, extended trust and awe to Wu and Hui; then gathered shields and spears, quieted Our border lands; Heaven and earth, ghosts and spirits, none did not obtain peace.
translations.idiomatic: You swept the land clear, carried awe to the Wu region, then put the weapons away and stilled Our borders until Heaven, earth, and the shades alike knew peace.

sentences.zh: 乃者王室之難，變起蕭牆，賴公之靈，弘濟艱險。

translations.literal: Then the royal house's hardship, change arose within the screen; relying on your numen, broadly crossed hardship and peril.
translations.idiomatic: When calamity struck within the palace screen, it was your guiding hand that carried the throne through the peril.

sentences.zh: 宗廟危而獲安，社稷墜而復寧。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple was perilous yet obtained peace; the altars of soil and grain fell yet again were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: The shrines tottered yet stood; the altars swayed yet steadied again.

sentences.zh: 忠格皇天，功濟六合。

translations.literal: Loyalty penetrates August Heaven; merit succors the six directions.
translations.idiomatic: Your loyalty reaches to Heaven; your service braces the whole world.

sentences.zh: 是用疇咨古訓，稽諸典籍，命公崇位相國，加於群後，啟土參墟，封以晉域。

translations.literal: Therefore We have questioned ancient instructions, examined the canons and records, ordered you to exalt position as Chancellor of State, added above the host of lords, opened soil at Sanxu, enfeoffed with the Jin domain.
translations.idiomatic: We have weighed the ancient precedents and the classics: We name you chancellor, set you above the other lords, and open the land of Sanxu as the state of Jin.

sentences.zh: 所以方軌齊魯，翰屏帝室。

translations.literal: By this means to parallel the tracks of Qi and Lu, be writing-screen to the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Thus you stand beside the great fiefs of Qi and Lu as a shield for the throne.

sentences.zh: 而公遠蹈謙損，深履沖讓，固辭策命，至於八九。

translations.literal: Yet you far tread modest yielding, deeply tread humble decline, firmly decline investiture commands, reaching to eight or nine times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have pressed humility to the utmost, refusing the patent of investiture eight or nine times running.

sentences.zh: 朕重違讓德，抑禮虧制，以彰公志，於今四載。

translations.literal: We heavily violate yielding virtue, suppress rite and diminish regulation, in order to display your intent; until now four years.
translations.idiomatic: We have long bent the rites to honor your modesty—four years now—yet the realm still lacks the fief your virtue deserves.

sentences.zh: 上闕在昔建侯之典，下違兆庶具瞻之望。

translations.literal: Above it lacks the canon of establishing marquises of old; below it violates the hundred million commoners' all-gazing hope.
translations.idiomatic: Above, We fail the ancient model of enfeoffing merit; below, We frustrate the people’s universal expectation.

sentences.zh: 惟公嚴虔王度，闡濟大猷，敦尚純樸，省繇節用，務穡勸分，九野康乂。

translations.literal: Only you sternly revere the king's measure, clarify and aid great plans, esteem and honor pure simplicity, reduce corvée and economize use, devote to harvest and encourage division, the nine fields are peaceful and governed.
translations.idiomatic: You uphold the royal statutes, open great policy, prize simplicity, cut levies and waste, urge farming and fair shares, until the nine provinces thrive in peace.

sentences.zh: 耆叟荷崇養之德，鰥寡蒙矜恤之施，仁風興於中夏，流澤布於遐荒。

translations.literal: Old men bear the virtue of exalted nurture; widowers and widows receive the application of pity and relief; humane wind rises in central Xia; flowing grace spreads to distant wastes.
translations.idiomatic: The aged enjoy your care, the lone and widowed your pity; a humane wind stirs in the heartland and your bounty reaches the farthest marches.

sentences.zh: 是以東夷西戎，南蠻北狄，狂狡貪悍，世為寇讎者，皆感義懷惠，款塞內附，或委命納貢，或求置官司。

translations.literal: Therefore eastern Yi, western Rong, southern Man, northern Di—wild, cunning, greedy, fierce, generation after generation enemies—all are moved by righteousness and cherish kindness, knock the passes and attach within, or cast mandate and present tribute, or request to set up offices.
translations.idiomatic: East and west, north and south, tribes long our foes now feel your justice and kindness; they crowd the passes with tribute or beg for offices under the throne.

sentences.zh: 九服之外，絕域之氓，曠世所希至者，咸浮海來享，鼓舞王德，前後至者八百七十餘萬口。

translations.literal: Beyond the nine domains, the wastes' commoners, those rare to reach in ages, all float the seas to come offer, drum and dance the king's virtue; before and after, arrivals exceed eight million seven hundred thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the nine circuits, peoples no envoy had reached for ages sail the seas to pay homage; in all, more than eight million seven hundred thousand souls have come.

sentences.zh: 海隅幽裔，無思不服；

translations.literal: Sea corners and dark descendants, none think and do not submit;
translations.idiomatic: Even the hidden corners of the coast bend the knee without prompting;

sentences.zh: 雖西旅遠貢，越裳九譯，義無以逾。

translations.literal: although Western Hosts' distant tribute, Yuechang's nine interpreters, in righteousness there is nothing to surpass.
translations.idiomatic: not since the Western Hosts or the nine-tongued envoys of Yuechang has fealty run deeper.

sentences.zh: 維翼朕躬，下匡萬國，思靖殊方，寧濟八極。

translations.literal: You wing Our person, below set aright the myriad states, think to quiet strange regions, pacify and succor the eight extremities.
translations.idiomatic: You brace Our person and steady every kingdom, seeking peace in strange lands and calm to the ends of the earth.

sentences.zh: 以庸蜀未賓，蠻荊作猾，潛謀獨斷，整軍經武。

translations.literal: Because Yong-Shu has not submitted, Man-Jing acts cunningly, you secretly plan alone and decide, array the army and regulate martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shu and Jing still withhold allegiance, you laid secret plans, mustered the host, and set the army in order.

sentences.zh: 簡練將帥，授以成策，始踐賊境，應時摧陷。

translations.literal: Selected and drilled generals and commanders, entrusted them completed stratagems; as soon as treading the bandit territory, in response to the moment smashed and fell.
translations.idiomatic: You picked and trained the commanders, gave them the finished plan, and the moment they set foot in enemy ground the foe collapsed.

sentences.zh: 狂狡奔北，首尾震潰，禽其戎帥，屠其城邑。

translations.literal: The wild and cunning fled north; head and tail quaked and routed; captured their war leaders, slaughtered their cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke and ran; van and rear alike shattered; you took their generals and stormed their towns.

sentences.zh: 巴漢震疊，江源雲徹，地平天成，誠在斯舉。

translations.literal: Ba and Han quaked in layers; Yangtze's source clouds cleared; earth level, Heaven completed—sincerity lies in this undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Ba and Han trembled, the river’s source opened like parting clouds; earth and Heaven align—and the deed is yours.

sentences.zh: 公有濟六合之勳，加以茂德，實總百揆，允厘庶政。

translations.literal: You have merit of succoring the six directions, added to luxuriant virtue; truly you overall command the hundred handles, truly you regulate the multitude of government.
translations.idiomatic: You have saved the realm and added brilliant virtue; you truly hold every rein of state and set all affairs straight.

sentences.zh: 敦五品以崇仁，恢六典以敷訓。

translations.literal: You urge the five grades to exalt benevolence; you enlarge the six canons to spread instruction.
translations.idiomatic: You nurture the five relationships toward humanity and spread the six statutes as the model for all.

sentences.zh: 而靖恭夙夜，勞謙昧旦，雖尚父之左右文武，周公之勤勞王家，罔以加焉。

translations.literal: Yet you are quiet and respectful early and late, toiling and humble before dawn; although the Grandfather's assisting left and right civil and martial, Duke of Zhou's toil for the royal house—nothing is added beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you rise in still reverence before dawn, humble in every task—not even the Grand Duke’s pairing of civil and martial, nor the Duke of Zhou’s zeal for the house, surpasses you.

sentences.zh: 昔先王選建明德，光啟諸侯，體國經野，方制五等。

translations.literal: In the past former kings selected and established bright virtue, broadly opened the feudal lords, embodied the state and regulated the wilds, thereby squared and established the five ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings chose men of bright virtue, opened fiefs for the lords, mapped state and wilderness, and fixed the five orders of nobility.

sentences.zh: 所以籓翼王畿，垂祚百世也。

translations.literal: By this means to screen and wing the royal domain, let blessings hang a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they shielded the royal domain and laid up fortune for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 故齊魯之封，于周為弘，山川土田，邦畿七百，官司典策，制殊群後。

translations.literal: Therefore Qi and Lu's enfeoffments, for Zhou were great; mountains, rivers, soil, fields—state domain seven hundred; offices, canons, and records—regulations differed from the host of lords.
translations.idiomatic: The grants to Qi and Lu were the greatest of Zhou: seven hundred li of hills, streams, and fields, with statutes and offices that set them apart from every other fief.

sentences.zh: 惠襄之難，桓文以翼戴之勞，猶受錫命之禮，咸用光疇大德，作范於後。

translations.literal: In Hui and Xiang's hardship, Huan and Wen by wing-and-cap labor still received the rite of bestowed commands; all used to brighten former great virtue, make model for later.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan and Wen saved the house of Zhou, they too received the nine gifts, that their great merit might shine as a pattern for posterity.

sentences.zh: 惟公功邁於前烈，而賞闕於舊式，百辟於邑，人神同恨焉，豈可以公謙沖而久淹弘典哉？

translations.literal: Only your merit surpasses former blazing deeds, yet reward lacks in old pattern; the hundred lords are anxious, man and spirit together resent—how can it be that because you are humble and yielding the grand canons are long submerged?
translations.idiomatic: Your deeds outshine the old exemplars, yet the old scale of reward has been withheld; lords and spirits alike chafe—can We forever hide the great statutes behind your modesty?

sentences.zh: 今以并州之太原上党西河樂平新興雁門、司州之河東平陽弘農、雍州之馮翊凡十郡，南至於華，北至於陘，東至於壺口，西逾於河，提封之數，方七百里，皆晉之故壤，唐叔受之，世作盟主，實紀綱諸夏，用率舊職。

translations.literal: Now with Bingzhou's Taiyuan, Shangdang, Xihe, Leping, Xinxing, Yanmen, and Sizhou's Hedong, Pingyang, Hongnong, and Yongzhou's Fengyi—altogether ten commanderies, south reaching to Hua, north reaching to Xing, east reaching to Hukou, west crossing beyond the River, the lifted-enclosure count, square seven hundred li—all are Jin's former soil, Tang Shu received it, generation after generation served as covenant lord, truly regulated the various Xia, thereby to follow old duties.
translations.idiomatic: We now grant ten commanderies—six of Bingzhou plus Hedong, Pingyang, Hongnong, and Fengyi—from Mount Hua in the south to Xing in the north, from Hukou in the east to the great River in the west, seven hundred li square: the ancient domain of Jin where Tang Shu once ruled as covenant lord of the Xia states. Take again that old charge.

sentences.zh: 爰胙茲土，封公為晉公。

translations.literal: Therefore enfeoff this soil, enfeoff you as Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore invest this soil and name you Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 命使持節、兼司徒、司隸校尉陔即授印綬策書，金獸符第一至第五，竹使符第一至第十。

translations.literal: Order Bearer of Credentials, concurrently Minister of Education, Metropolitan Commandant immediately to confer seal-ribbon and patent text, gold beast tallies first through fifth, bamboo envoy tallies first through tenth.
translations.idiomatic: We send a credential bearer, concurrent Minister of Education and metropolitan commandant, to hand you seal, ribbon, patent, gold beast tallies one through five, and bamboo tallies one through ten.

sentences.zh: 錫茲玄土，苴以白茅，建爾國家，以永籓魏室。

translations.literal: Bestow this dark soil, wrap with white rushes, establish your state and house, thereby forever to screen the Wei house.
translations.idiomatic: We grant you this black earth bound with white rushes; found your state and be a lasting shield for Wei.

sentences.zh: 昔在周召，並以公侯，入作保傅。

translations.literal: In the past at Zhou and Shao, both by duke and marquis rank, entered to serve as protector and tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Of old the dukes of Zhou and Shao entered court as dukes and marquises to serve as regents.

sentences.zh: 其在近代，酂侯蕭何，實以相國，光尹漢朝。

translations.literal: In recent times, Marquis of Zan Xiao He, truly by minister of state, brightly governed Han court.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages Marquis Xiao He as chancellor lit the Han court with his rule.

sentences.zh: 隨時之制，禮亦宜之。

translations.literal: Following the season's regulation, rite also fits it.
translations.idiomatic: Rites shift with the times, and this grant fits the hour.

sentences.zh: 今進公位為相國，加綠綟綬。

translations.literal: Now advance your position to Chancellor of State, add green-and-black ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: We now advance you to chancellor and add the green-and-black ribbon of that office.

sentences.zh: 又加公九錫，其敬聽後命。

translations.literal: Again add to you the nine bestowals; respectfully listen to the later commands.
translations.idiomatic: We add the nine gifts; hear now the items that follow.

sentences.zh: 以公思弘大猷，崇正典禮，儀刑作範，旁訓四方，是用錫公大輅、戎輅各一，玄牡二駟。

translations.literal: Because you think to enlarge great plans, exalt and correct canons and rites, model and make pattern, broadly instruct the four quarters, therefore We bestow on you great chariot and war chariot each one, dark male teams two four-horse teams.
translations.idiomatic: Because you widen great policy, uphold the rites, and set the pattern for the four quarters, We grant you the state chariot and the war chariot, each with a team of four black stallions.

sentences.zh: 公道和陰陽，敬授人時，嗇夫反本，農殖維豐，是用錫公袞冕之服，赤舄副焉。

translations.literal: You harmonize Yin and Yang, reverently grant men their seasons; farmers return to root, farming increase is luxuriant; therefore We bestow on you robe and crown of state, red slippers accompanying.
translations.idiomatic: Because you harmonize Yin and Yang, set the calendar, and send farmers back to the soil until the harvests run rich, We grant the sacral robes and crown with the red court shoes.

sentences.zh: 公光敷顯德，惠下以和，敬信思順，庶尹允諧，是用錫公軒懸之樂、六佾之舞。

translations.literal: You brightly spread manifest virtue, show kindness below with harmony, reverent trust thinks compliance; myriad directors truly harmonize; therefore We bestow on you suspended hall music and six-row dance.
translations.idiomatic: Because your virtue shines abroad and every office moves in harmony, We grant you the graded bells and the six rows of dancers.

sentences.zh: 公鎮靖宇宙，翼播聲教，海外懷服，荒裔款附，殊方馳義，諸夏順軌，是用錫公硃戶以居。

translations.literal: You pacify and quiet the cosmos within the four seas, wing and spread sound and teaching; beyond the seas they cherish submission; distant wastes knock in attachment; strange regions gallop righteousness; the various Xia follow the track; therefore We bestow on you vermilion doors to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Because you still the world and carry civilization to the seas, until distant lands submit, We grant vermilion lacquer for your gates.

sentences.zh: 公簡賢料材，營求俊逸，爰升多士，置彼周行，是用錫公納陛以登。

translations.literal: You select worthies and measure talent, seek and recruit outstanding; then raise many gentlemen, set them in that Zhou road; therefore We bestow on you inner stair to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Because you choose the able and set them in the king’s highway, We grant the inner stair by which you mount the hall.

sentences.zh: 公嚴恭寅畏，底平四國，式遏寇虐，苛厲不作，是用錫公武賁之士三百人。

translations.literal: You sternly revere and fear respectfully, settle and level the four states, pattern-block bandit cruelty; harsh severity does not arise; therefore We bestow on you three hundred martial fierce gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Because you awe the four quarters and stop cruelty without harshness, We grant three hundred picked guards of the martial escort.

sentences.zh: 公明慎用刑，簡恤大中，章厥天威，以糾不虔，是用錫公鈇鉞各一。

translations.literal: You are enlightened and cautious in employing punishments, select and pity the great center, display that Heaven's majesty, thereby to correct what is not reverent; therefore We bestow on you axe and yue each one.
translations.idiomatic: Because you use punishments with care and display Heaven’s awe against the impious, We grant the execution axe and the ceremonial yue.

sentences.zh: 公爰整六軍，典司征伐，犯命淩正，乃維誅殛，是用錫公彤弓一、彤矢百，玈弓十、玈矢千。

translations.literal: You then array the six armies, take charge of campaigning and punishing; those who violate commands and encroach the upright, then are to be executed and slain; therefore We bestow on you one red bow, one hundred red arrows, ten black bows, one thousand black arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Because you command the six hosts and strike down every violator of the king’s command, We grant the red bow with a hundred arrows and ten black bows with a thousand shafts.

sentences.zh: 公饗祀蒸蒸，孝思維則，篤誠之至，通於神明，是用錫公秬鬯一卣，圭瓚副焉。

translations.literal: You feast-sacrifice steaming, filial thought takes them as model; utmost sincere arrival penetrates to spirits and gods; therefore We bestow on you one you of black millet ale, jade ladle accompanying.
translations.idiomatic: Because your ancestral rites rise in steam and your filial heart moves the spirits, We grant a jar of dark ale with the jade libation spoon.

sentences.zh: 晉國置官司以下，率由舊式。

translations.literal: For the Jin state, establishing offices downward, all follow old pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The offices of the state of Jin shall follow the old forms.

sentences.zh: 往欽哉！

translations.literal: Go, reverently!
translations.idiomatic: Go—and be reverent!

sentences.zh: 祗服朕命，弘敷訓典，光澤庶方，永終爾明德，丕顯餘一人之休命。

translations.literal: Reverently submit to Our command, broadly spread instruction and canons, brighten and moisten the myriad regions, eternally end your bright virtue, greatly display Our solitary person's fine command.
translations.idiomatic: Accept Our charge, spread the teaching, bring light to every quarter, let your bright virtue endure, and magnify this sovereign’s gracious word.

sentences.zh: 公卿將校皆詣府喻旨，帝以禮辭讓。

translations.literal: Dukes, ministers, generals, and colonels all went to the mansion to explain the intent; the Emperor by rite declined.
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers and commanders crowded his gate with the edict; he declined again by formal courtesy.

sentences.zh: 司空鄭沖率群官勸進曰：「伏見嘉命顯至，竊聞明公固讓，沖等眷眷，實有愚心。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zheng Chong led the host of officials to urge advance saying: We humbly see the fine command clearly arrived; we privately hear the enlightened lord firmly declines; Chong and others are attached, truly having foolish hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chong led the officials in a memorial of urging that the gracious command had come yet they heard the lord refuse, and that they could not rest for worry.

sentences.zh: 以為聖王作制，百代同風，褒德賞功，有自來矣。

translations.literal: We consider that the sage king makes institutions; a hundred generations share one wind; praising virtue and rewarding merit has had its source from of old.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings set precedent for every age: to honor merit is the way of antiquity itself.

sentences.zh: 昔伊尹，有莘氏之媵臣耳，一佐成湯，遂荷阿衡之號。

translations.literal: In the past Yi Yin was only Youxin's accompanying minister; once he assisted Cheng Tang, then he bore the title of Ah Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin began as a mere attendant of Youxin; one service to Tang won him the name Ah Heng.

sentences.zh: 周公藉已成之勢，據既安之業，光宅曲阜，奄有龜蒙。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou leaned on already completed power, occupied already secure enterprise, brightly dwelt at Qufu, covered Gui and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou took power already won and a realm already calm, then made Qufu his seat and held Gui and Meng.

sentences.zh: 呂尚，磻溪之漁者也，一朝指麾，乃封營丘。

translations.literal: Lü Shang was a fisherman of Panxi; one morning directing and waving, then was enfeoffed at Yingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shang was a fisherman by Pan Creek; one morning’s command won him Yingqiu.

sentences.zh: 自是以來，功薄而賞厚者，不可勝數，然賢哲之士，猶以為美談。

translations.literal: From this onward, those whose merit was thin yet reward was thick cannot be counted; yet worthy and wise gentlemen still take them as fine tales.
translations.idiomatic: Since then thin merit has often drawn rich reward—yet wise men still praise those tales.

sentences.zh: 況自先相國以來，世有明德，翼輔魏室，以綏天下，朝無秕政，人無謗言。

translations.literal: Moreover since the former Chancellor of State, generation after generation there has been bright virtue, winging and assisting the Wei house, thereby pacifying all under Heaven; court has no chaff government, men have no slanderous words.
translations.idiomatic: From your grandfather the chancellor onward, each generation has aided Wei with shining virtue until the court is clean of chaff and the people free of slander.

sentences.zh: 前者明公西征靈州，北臨沙漠，榆中以西，望風震服，羌戎來馳，回首內向，東誅叛逆，全軍獨克。

translations.literal: Formerly the enlightened lord west campaigned Lingzhou, north faced the desert; west of Yuzhong, gazing at the wind trembled and submitted; Qiang and Rong came galloping, turned head inward; east punished rebels and traitors, whole army alone overcame.
translations.idiomatic: You marched west to Lingzhou and north to the sands; west of Yuzhong every tribe trembled into submission; Qiang and Rong wheeled their horses toward the throne; in the east you cut down rebels alone and whole.

sentences.zh: 禽闔閭之將，虜輕銳之卒以萬萬計，威加南海，名懾三越，宇內康寧，苛慝不作。

translations.literal: Captured Helü's generals, took light keen soldiers by the ten thousands counted; awe added to South Sea, name overawed the three Yues; within the four seas peaceful and tranquil, harsh evil did not arise.
translations.idiomatic: You took Wu’s generals and tens of thousands of their best troops, spread terror to the Southern Sea and the three Yues, and brought peace so that cruelty died away.

sentences.zh: 是以時俗畏懷，東夷獻舞。

translations.literal: Therefore the age's customs feared and cherished; eastern Yi presented dance.
translations.idiomatic: The age stands in awe; even the eastern Yi send dancers to your court.

sentences.zh: 故聖上覽乃昔以來禮典舊章，開國光宅，顯茲太原。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage superior surveys thence past rites and canons, old regulations, opens state and bright dwelling, displays this Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage Son of Heaven has weighed the old statutes and opened a bright fief for you at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 明公宜承奉聖旨，受茲介福，允當天人。

translations.literal: The enlightened lord ought to receive and follow the sage decree, receive this great blessing, truly meet Heaven and men.
translations.idiomatic: You should accept the imperial word, take this great blessing, and satisfy both Heaven and the people.

sentences.zh: 元功盛勳，光光如彼；

translations.literal: Founding merit and blazing achievement, blazingly thus;
translations.idiomatic: Your founding merit shines so bright;

sentences.zh: 國土嘉祚，巍巍如此。

translations.literal: State soil and fine blessing, thus lofty.
translations.idiomatic: the fief and fortune offered you stand so high.

sentences.zh: 內外協同，靡愆靡違。

translations.literal: Inner and outer join in harmony; none fault, none violate.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without all move as one, without fault or breach.

sentences.zh: 由斯征伐，則可朝服濟江，掃除吳會，西塞江源，望祀岷山。

translations.literal: From this campaigning, then can in court robes cross the Yangtze, sweep and clear Wu and Hui, west block Yangtze's source, gaze-sacrifice Mount Min.
translations.idiomatic: With that you may cross the Yangzi in court dress, sweep Wu clean, seal the river’s upper course, and offer the rite on Mount Min.

sentences.zh: 回戈弭節，以麾天下，遠無不服，邇無不肅。

translations.literal: Turn halberd and still the baton, thereby to command all under Heaven; far none not submit, near none not solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Then lay by spear and still the reins to command the realm until the far submit and the near stand in awe.

sentences.zh: 令大魏之德，光于唐虞；

translations.literal: Let great Wei's virtue shine on Tang and Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei’s virtue will outshine Tang and Yu;

sentences.zh: 明公盛勳，超于桓文。

translations.literal: the enlightened lord's blazing merit surpasses Huan and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: and your merit will rise above Huan and Wen.

sentences.zh: 然後臨滄海而謝支伯，登箕山而揖許由，豈不盛乎！

translations.literal: Then facing the dark sea and thanking Zhibo, ascending Mount Ji and bowing to Xu You—is it not grand!
translations.idiomatic: Then you might stand by the eastern sea as kings of old did before worthy recluses, or climb Mount Ji to salute Xu You—what could be more glorious!

sentences.zh: 至公至平，誰與為鄰，何必勤勤小讓也哉。

translations.literal: Utmost public-mindedness, utmost fairness—who stands as neighbor; why must one be diligent in petty yielding?
translations.idiomatic: You have reached perfect equity—none can stand beside you—so why cling to these small courtesies of refusal?

sentences.zh: 」帝乃受命。

translations.literal: The Emperor then received the command.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao then accepted.

sentences.zh: 十一月，鄧艾帥萬餘人自陰平逾絕險至江由，破蜀將諸葛瞻於綿竹，斬瞻，傳首。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Deng Ai led more than ten thousand from Yinping crossing extreme peril to reach Jiangyou, defeated Shu general Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu, beheaded Zhan, sent the head by relay.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Deng Ai took ten thousand men over the sheer track from Yinping to Jiangyou, crushed Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu, struck off his head, and sent it east by post.

sentences.zh: 進軍雒縣，劉禪降。

translations.literal: Advanced the army to Luo county; Liu Shan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to Luo county, and Liu Shan yielded.

sentences.zh: 天子命晉公以相國總百揆，於是上節傳，去侍中、大都督、錄尚書之號焉。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered the Duke of Jin by Chancellor of State to overall command the hundred handles; thereupon he submitted credentials and tallies, removed Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and recording Director of the Secretariat titles.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named the Duke of Jin chancellor with full authority over the government; Sima Zhao thereupon returned his batons and dropped the concurrent titles of Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and overseer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 表鄧艾為太尉，鐘會為司徒。

translations.literal: He memorialized Deng Ai as Grand Commandant, Zhong Hui as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Deng Ai for Grand Commandant and Zhong Hui for Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 會潛謀叛逆，因密使譖艾。

translations.literal: Hui secretly plotted rebellion, thereby secretly sent to slander Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui plotted revolt in secret and sent agents to traduce Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 咸熙元年春正月，檻車征艾。

translations.literal: First year of Xianxi, spring, first month, caged cart summoned Ai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Xianxi year 1, Deng Ai was summoned back in a prison cart.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，帝奉天子西征，次於長安。

translations.literal: On yichou, the Emperor escorting the Son of Heaven west campaigned, halted at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he escorted the emperor west and encamped at Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 是時魏諸王侯悉在鄴城，命從事中郎山濤行軍司事，鎮於鄴，遣護軍賈充持節、督諸軍，據漢中。

translations.literal: At this time Wei various princes and marquises were all at Yecheng; he ordered Retainer Shan Tao to conduct army affairs, garrisoning at Yecheng; sent Army Protector Jia Chong bearing credentials, supervising the various armies, occupying Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: With every Wei prince gathered at Yecheng, he put Shan Tao in charge of rear-area command there and sent Jia Chong with baton to oversee the armies holding Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 鐘會遂反於蜀，監軍衛瓘、右將軍胡烈攻會，斬之。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui then rebelled in Shu; Army Supervisor Wei Guan, General of the Right Hu Lie attacked Hui, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui rose in Shu; Wei Guan and Hu Lie struck him down and took his head.

sentences.zh: 初，會之伐蜀也，西曹屬邵悌言於帝曰：「鐘會難信，不可令行。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Hui campaigned against Shu, Western Bureau Subordinate Shao Ti spoke to the Emperor saying: "Zhong Hui is hard to trust; cannot let him march.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui first marched on Shu, Shao Ti of the Western Bureau had warned Sima Zhao that Zhong Hui was not to be trusted and must not be given independent command.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「取蜀如指掌，而眾人皆言不可，唯會與吾意同。

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "Taking Shu is like pointing at the palm; yet the host of men all say it cannot be done; only Hui and Our intent agree.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao had only smiled and said, "Shu will fall as easily as reading one’s palm, though everyone else doubted—only Zhong Hui shared my view."

sentences.zh: 滅蜀之後，中國將士，人自思歸，蜀之遺黎，猶懷震恐，縱有異志，無能為也。

translations.literal: After extinguishing Shu, central state's officers and soldiers, each person thinks of returning; Shu's surviving common people still cherish trembling fear; even if they had different intent, they have no ability to act.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell, every northern soldier would pine for home and the Shu populace would still quake with fear—even if someone harbored treason, he could do nothing with it.

sentences.zh: 」卒如所量。

translations.literal: In the end it was as he had measured.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved him exactly right.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝至自長安。

translations.literal: On bingchen, the Emperor arrived from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he returned from Chang’an to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三月己卯，進帝爵為王，增封並前二十郡。

translations.literal: Third month, day jimao, advanced the Emperor's noble rank to king, increased fief together with the previous twenty commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao in the third month he was raised from duke to king with twenty commanderies in all, old grants and new.

sentences.zh: 夏五月癸未，天子追加舞陽宣文侯為晉宣王，舞陽忠武侯為晉景王。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day guiwei, the Son of Heaven posthumously added Wuyang Marquis Xuanwen as Jin King Xuan, Wuyang Marquis Zhongwu as Jin King Jing.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei in the fifth month of summer the emperor posthumously raised Sima Yi to Prince Xuan of Jin and Sima Shi to Prince Jing of Jin.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，帝奏司空荀顗定禮儀，中護軍賈充正法律，尚書僕射裴秀議官制，太保鄭沖總而裁焉。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, the Emperor memorialized Minister of Works Xun Yi to fix rites and ceremonies, Central Army Protector Jia Chong to rectify laws and statutes, Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu to deliberate official system, Grand Guardian Zheng Chong overall to judge them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he charged Xun Yi with the rites, Jia Chong with the laws, Pei Xiu with the bureaucracy, and Zheng Chong as coordinator over all.

sentences.zh: 始建五等爵。

translations.literal: For the first time established the five ranks of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: He began the institution of the five orders of nobility.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁亥，奏遣吳人相國參軍徐劭、散騎常侍水曹屬孫彧使吳，喻孫皓以平蜀之事，致馬錦等物，以示威懷。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day dinghai, memorialized to send Wu man Chancellor of State Army Advisor Xu Shao, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Water Bureau Subordinate Sun Yu as envoys to Wu, informing Sun Hao of the affair of pacifying Shu, presenting horses, brocade, and such objects, in order to show awe and cherishing.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai in the tenth winter month he memorialized to send Xu Shao and Sun Yu—Wu natives in his service—to Wu with horses and brocade, to tell Sun Hao of Shu’s fall and to blend threat with kindness.

sentences.zh: 丙午，天子命中撫軍新昌鄉侯炎為晉世子。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Son of Heaven ordered Central General Who Stabilizes the Army, village marquis of Xinchang Yan, to be Jin heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the emperor named Sima Yan, the Central Stabilizing General and Marquis of Xinchang township, heir to the duchy of Jin.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月甲辰，朐縣獻靈龜，歸於相府。

translations.literal: Second year, spring, second month, day jiachen, Qu county presented a numinous tortoise; it was sent to the chancellor's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen in the second month of spring, the second year, Qu county sent up a sacred tortoise to the chancellor’s residence.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，孫皓使紀陟來聘，且獻方物。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, Sun Hao sent Ji Zhi to come on friendly mission, and also present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Sun Hao sent Ji Zhi on a goodwill embassy with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五月，天子命帝冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕，樂舞八佾，設鐘虡宮懸，位在燕王上。

translations.literal: Fifth month, the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor's crown twelve tassels, erected Son of Heaven banners and flags, going out cleared roads entering cordoned progress, riding gold-root carriage, driving six horses, prepared five-seasons secondary carriages, set up yak-tail pennants and cloud-net banners, music and dance eight rows, established bell-stands palace suspended music, rank above the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor granted him the twelve-tassel crown, imperial banners, cleared roads for his comings and goings, the gold-wheeled carriage drawn by six horses, five seasonal escort chariots, yak-tail and cloud banners, eight rows of dancers, bell-chimes in the palace style, and precedence above the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 進王妃為王后，世子為太子，王女王孫爵命之號皆如帝者之儀。

translations.literal: Advanced the prince's consort to queen, heir apparent to crown prince; prince's daughters and grandsons' noble title commands all as the Son of Heaven's ritual.
translations.idiomatic: His consort became queen, his heir crown prince, and the titles for his daughters and grandsons matched those of the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 諸禁網煩苛及法式不便於時者，帝皆奏除之。

translations.literal: Various prohibitions, nets, vexing harshness, and legal models not convenient to the age—the Emperor all memorialized to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to repeal every harsh prohibition and obsolete statute that burdened the times.

sentences.zh: 晉國置御史大夫、侍中、常侍、尚書、中領軍、衛將軍官。

translations.literal: The Jin state established Censor-in-chief, Palace Attendant, Regular Attendant, Director, Central Army Supervisor, General of the Guard offices.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Jin was given a full set of offices—censor-in-chief, attendants, secretariat directors, central army supervisor, and general of the guard.

sentences.zh: 秋八月辛卯，帝崩於露寢，時年五十五。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day xinmao, the Emperor died in the open hall; at the time his years were fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the open hall on xinmao in the eighth month of autumn, aged fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 九月癸酉，葬崇陽陵，諡曰文王。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day guiyou, buried at Chongyang Mausoleum; posthumous name King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou in the ninth month he was buried at Chongyang Mausoleum with the posthumous title Wen, the Cultured King.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，追尊號曰文皇帝，廟稱太祖。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, posthumously honored title as Emperor Wen, temple called Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne, Sima Zhao was posthumously raised to Emperor Wen with the temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：世宗以睿略創基，太祖以雄才成務。

translations.literal: The history official says: Shizong by keen strategy founded the base; Taizu by heroic talent completed the task.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Emperor Shi founded the enterprise with cunning strategy, and Emperor Tai completed it with heroic force.

sentences.zh: 事殷之跡空存，翦商之志彌遠，三分天下，功業在焉。

translations.literal: The traces of serving Yin empty survive; the intent to cut Shang grows more distant; dividing three parts the realm, merit and enterprise lie therein.
translations.idiomatic: The mask of serving the house of Cao grew ever thinner while the will to supplant it burned brighter; they split the realm three ways, and there lay their achievement.

sentences.zh: 及逾劍銷氛，浮淮靜亂，桐宮胥怨，或所不堪。

translations.literal: When it came to crossing the sword to dispel miasma, floating the Huai to quiet rebellion, Tong Palace all resented—perhaps what could not be borne.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Sword Gates to end the fog of war, rode the Huai to crush revolt—yet the bitterness of the Tong-palace depositions was more than some could stomach.

sentences.zh: 若乃體以名臣，格之端揆，周公流連於此歲，魏武得意於茲日。

translations.literal: If then embodying by famous ministers, patterning by chief ministers—Duke of Zhou lingered in this year, Wei Wu was pleased on this day.
translations.idiomatic: Set beside the great ministers of old and the chief arbiters of policy, their course recalls the Duke of Zhou’s long season of care and the day Cao Cao seized his own triumph.

sentences.zh: 軒懸之樂，大啟南陽，師摯之圖，於焉北面。

translations.literal: Suspended hall music, greatly opened Nanyang; Master Zhi's chart, thereupon faced north.
translations.idiomatic: The graded bells of state sounded from Nanyang, and the royal musicians turned their registers toward the northern court.

sentences.zh: 壯矣哉，包舉天人者也！

translations.literal: Grand indeed! They who wrap and raise Heaven and man!
translations.idiomatic: Magnificent—they took Heaven and humanity both in their grasp!

sentences.zh: 為帝之主，不亦難乎。

translations.literal: To be lord of emperors—is it not also difficult?
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder that holding the title of emperor proved no easy thing.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：世宗繼文，邦權未分。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Shizong continued Wen; state power not yet divided.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Emperor Shi followed the cultured king, while the power of the state still hung undivided.

sentences.zh: 三千之士，其從如雲。

translations.literal: Three thousand gentlemen—their following like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand retainers followed them like clouds.

sentences.zh: 世祖無外，靈關靜氛。

translations.literal: Shizu without those outside; spirit passes quiet miasma.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu Sima Yan came, no foe stood beyond the pale and the sacred passes fell still.

sentences.zh: 反雖討賊，終為弑君。

translations.literal: Although turning back punished bandits, in the end it was regicide of the lord.
translations.idiomatic: Though they struck in the name of punishing traitors, in the end they slew their king.
